News.title: Man sniffed out by police dog while hiding behind fake wall on 300-plant cannabis farm
News.content:
A man has been jailed for six months after being found by a sniffer dog behind a fake wall on a cannabis farm.

Albert Hysaj, 42, pleaded guilty to producing cannabis and was sentenced at Cardiff Crown Court on Friday.

Hysaj was caught after a police dog named Asko located him in the commercial property on the Bowen Industrial Estate, in Aberbargoed, Caerphilly county, in May.

Gwent Police found 313 cannabis plants inside two linked units over three rooms, which included a living area with kitchen and bathroom.

News.title: Presenter Tony Livesey leaves BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years
News.content:
Presenter Tony Livesey has left BBC Radio 5 Live after 16 years at the station, the corporation has announced.

Livesey stepped back from his weekday late night talk show in June, following allegations made against his former newspaper boss David Sullivan.

He had previously worked as editor-in-chief of Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport publications.

Several women have accused Sullivan, a billionaire businessman and West Ham co-owner, of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were teenagers. Sullivan has strongly denied the allegations.

The claims against Sullivan were made in a joint investigation by the Times and BBC Panorama.

The BBC previously said Livesey had asked to take a break from presenting his programme while the issues raised by the investigation were being examined.

One alleged victim said that Livesey had arranged a meeting between her and Sullivan in 1999.

Livesey said he had "no recollection" of introducing the young woman to Sullivan and that it was "not part" of his job to do so.

He added that he had "great sympathy for a woman who may have become a victim", but rejected any suggestion that he had played "any role whatsoever in that scenario" and said he found the allegation "abhorrent".

In an email sent to 5 Live staff on Monday morning, the station's controller Heidi Dawson said he had now decided to leave.

"Tony has asked me to pass on his heartfelt thanks to the brilliant colleagues at 5 Live who he has had the pleasure of working with over the years," she wrote.

"I know many of you have also really enjoyed working with Tony, and we wish him well for all his future endeavours."

The award-winning presenter worked for the BBC from 2006 - the same year he left the newspapers - appearing on 5 Live from 2010 onwards, including a successful stint hosting its drivetime show.

He won radio awards - ARIA and APAs - for his reporting on how it feels to lose your mother as a child, and an ARIAS gold award after he was asked by the late Dame Deborah James to conduct her final interview.

His topical three-hour programme was broadcast on 5 Live from Monday to Thursday, featuring interviews and phone calls from listeners.

It started with Instagram posts that suggested Spain’s border with Morocco was opening up. Then came Facebook users tracking coast guard patrols and TikTok videos showing where to swim.

After many shares and comments, thousands of Moroccans became convinced that Europe was suddenly within reach.

Within hours, young people began heading toward the border with the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in North Africa. Packed buses rolled into the neighboring Moroccan city of Fnideq. Regional trains filled up. Taxis did too.

By the time authorities reacted, an estimated 60,000 people had reached Ceuta in just a few days, the largest migration surge between Morocco and Spain in years. More than 80 migrants died on both sides of the border, including some who drowned and others who were killed in a stampede, authorities said.

Nearly all of the surviving migrants soon returned, but the fallout from last week’s events will linger.

Rumors started online

In the northern Moroccan city of Larache, about 93 miles (150 kilometers) from Ceuta, three friends watched a video posted by an Instagram account called Haraga Ceuta claiming the border would be open. Haraga refers in Moroccan dialect to young migrants who destroy their identification papers and try crossing illegally into Europe.

The post convinced Anas Amrani, Yahya Harak and Ismail Atik that it was worth risking the journey.

For migrants hoping to reach Spanish territory, the most common route begins in Fnideq, where many attempt the roughly 3-mile (5-kilometer) swim around the border breakwater. Others leave from the nearby village of Belyounech.

One TikTok video mapped the exact route swimmers should follow.

On Facebook groups such as Fnideq Bab Sebta, users shared screenshots from vessel-tracking platforms to identify moments when coast guard patrols appeared lighter. Some sought advice on using inflatable boats. Others advertised wetsuits for sale.

“I saw online that the border was open, and I decided to go,” said 17-year-old Omar Danbor from Fnideq, walking back exhausted along the coast.

It's unclear who was behind the claims that the border was open or who operated many of the social media accounts, several of which were deleted soon after the crossings. The Associated Press contacted several accounts but received no response.

Chaos at the breakwater

As migrants reached the shores of Ceuta, mass chaos erupted at a narrow concrete breakwater where many tried to climb onto land.

According to multiple migrants interviewed by AP, people rushed to scramble over the slick rocks at the same time, pushing and climbing over one another. Several said they saw people knocked back into the water and forced beneath others, leaving them unable to resurface as migrants sought to reach land.

“I stepped on the face of a dead man while I was climbing out. I hope God forgives me and all those whose bodies were found,” said Lahcen Kalouch, a Moroccan migrant who reached Ceuta before returning home distraught.

At least 72 people died on the Spanish side of the border. Another 11 died on the Moroccan side.

Tens of thousands of migrants have since returned to Morocco, either after being expelled or after leaving by choice because of a lack of shelter, food and water in Ceuta.

Some misinterpreted Spain’s new migration measures

Some migrants misunderstood recent legal developments in Spain, including Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s immigration regularization measures and a court ruling limiting authorities’ ability to immediately return migrants who swim into Ceuta.

Sanchez’s recent efforts to regularize migration were meant only for people already living in Spain prior to Jan. 1, the majority of whom hail from Latin America and entered Spain legally but overstayed their visas. But some in Morocco misinterpreted his policy, believing they would be allowed to stay. That belief spread online.

“Pedro Sánchez is a liar. He told us if we came, we would get jobs and papers, but they sent us back,” said Adam Assil, a migrant from Casablanca, even though Sánchez never made such a promise.

While attempts to reach Ceuta are common, migration activists said this episode was different because of the way rumors snowballed online, encouraging thousands of people to head toward the enclave at the same time instead of in smaller, scattered groups.

Failures happened on both sides of the border

Moroccan authorities said the migration wave was not spontaneous. The Interior Ministry blamed the “exploitation of the digital sphere” and “the spread of misinformation.” Officials offered no evidence but said an investigation had been opened. Spain’s government made similar statements.

Ceuta officials said that they had warned the Spanish government of a surge in arrivals before the massive crush on Thursday. The Spanish Interior Ministry said Monday that it had not received “any report or warning regarding the mass arrival of people in Ceuta,” and it praised cooperation with the Moroccan authorities in sending most of the migrants back.

“Nobody addressed how these individuals managed to breach the border," said Mustapha Azaitraoui, a Moroccan geographer specializing in migration dynamics. “If a large group of people can cross the border under these circumstances, it suggests a broader security issue that has yet to be acknowledged publicly.”

Migrants reject government claims of smuggling

Both Morocco and Spain blamed the Ceuta crisis on human smugglers and trafficking networks, saying organized criminal groups encouraged the mass crossings.

But returning Moroccan migrants interviewed by AP largely rejected that explanation.

“No one smuggled me there. I wanted to go of my own free will, but that country is not worth all this sacrifice,” Kalouch said.

“There are no mafias. The border was open, and I crossed. But now I regret it,” said Danbor, his clothes still wet after making the journey back.

The Spanish Interior Ministry said investigations into smuggling networks are ongoing and noted that Spain and Morocco have carried out joint operations against trafficking groups. The Moroccan Interior Ministry did not respond to questions about smuggling networks.

Lack of jobs is a key factor

Morocco’s economy is projected to grow by 4.5% this year, boasting major factories, advanced ports and ambitions to become a regional hub for the car industry.

Yet for many young Moroccans, that transformation has not translated into stable work. Youth unemployment remains high, with 37% of people ages 15 to 24 out of work. Among university graduates, unemployment stands at nearly 20%. The dream of migration is often reinforced by stories of relatives who left and returned with cars, new clothes and foreign currency.

One of those who breached the border was a 16-year-old who grew up a few dozen miles from Ceuta. Europe had always seemed a dream close enough to see, yet impossibly far.

So when he saw a post on Facebook suggesting the border was open and thousands were making it across, he joined the rush.

Days later, he was back on the Moroccan side, crying as he asked strangers for money for a taxi home.

“They fired tear gas at me and beat me with batons. There’s nothing for me there,” said the teen, who spoke on condition of anonymity out of fear of being stigmatized following his failed border crossing attempt.

“I just wanted to provide for my mom,” he said, wiping his tears.

___

Associated Press journalists Bernat Armangue in Ceuta, Spain, and Joseph Wilson in Barcelona, Spain, contributed.

Investors in Elon Musk's space company get a chance to question him Tuesday after SpaceX issues its first quarterly earnings since going public.

SpaceX shares are down by half from their June peak as investors worry Musk may have oversold them on its future prospects. They're also bracing for volatile trading as some company insiders get the opportunity to sell shares after the expiration of what's known as a lockup provision later in the week.

Part visionary engineer, part stock salesman, Musk is likely to be asked about when he expects to finish testing SpaceX's giant Starship rockets that NASA hopes to use to put men on the moon again, his plans for its satellite network and the prospects of putting football-field sized datacenters in orbit.

Given rumors of SpaceX possibly merging with Musk's Tesla car company, he may also face questions about that tie-up but that is likely to yield few details. Neither company has confirmed plans for a combination and Musk has parried questions before by noting securities regulations bar him from discussing the issue.

SpaceX is losing money fast, with net losses for its first half this year expected to exceed more than the $5 billion in losses for all of last year. Some analysts have penciled in a strong rebound for the rest of the year that will return it to profitability.

For the second quarter ended June, SpaceX is expected to report a net loss of $1.9 billion, or 23 cents a share, according to a FactSet survey of analysts.

SpaceX insiders were barred from selling in the public offering in June but that prohibition begins to ease on Thursday when more than 900,000 shares are released for trading, more than doubling the amount currently available for trading. The prospect has weighed on the shares, which closed Monday at $114.46, down from both the peak of $225 in June and also the IPO price of $135.

The lockup release is the first of several tranches of stock that will be freed to trade over the next several months.

After an abandoned launch, the Starship rocket successfully deployed satellites in orbit during a test late last month. Future tests could include trying to use giant arms at its Starbase launching site in Texas to grab the rocket and its booster upon its hovering return to earth.

SpaceX's satellite communication business, Starlink, is a big cash generator for the company with contracts around the world. The company also runs a money-losing AI business, known for its Grok tool, as well as the social media platform X, the rennamed Twitter.

Asian shares mostly declined Tuesday, despite a rally on Wall Street boosted by easing oil prices, as regional investors still weighed the impact from the recent joint U.S.-Japan currency intervention.

Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 63,369.85, as the U.S. dollar inched up to 157.63 Japanese yen from 157.18 yen. The euro cost $1.1511, little changed from $1.1514. The dollar was trading at 160-yen levels before the intervention.

Some analysts said the effectiveness of such an intervention remains uncertain as it doesn't address the fundamental economic reasons behind the currency fluctuations, including inflation, interest rates and the relative strengths of the economies.

“A U.S.-backed operation carries far more signaling weight than Tokyo acting alone, and the pledge of further action will give speculators pause. But any U.S. contribution will probably be constrained by size,” a report by BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, said.

Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at global financial services firm Ebury, noted the latest effort could have some impact because it appears to signal a real change in monetary policy rather than just a one-time defensive move.

“This is an historic and meaningful development for the yen, which materially improves confidence in our mildly bullish call for the currency,” he said.

South Korea's Kospi inched down less than 0.1% to 6,254.76. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 added 1.2% to 9,128.60. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.5% to 25,881.99, while the Shanghai Composite declined 0.2% to 3,802.61.

On Wall Street, share prices rallied Monday after easing oil prices helped calm worries that inflation could get even worse. The S&P 500 jumped 1.5% and is just 0.1% below its record set earlier this summer.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which measures a narrower slice of the U.S. stock market, climbed 693 points or 1.3% to an all-time high, while the Nasdaq composite leaped 2.1%.

In energy trading in Asia early Tuesday, benchmark U.S. crude gained 50 cents to $80.84 a barrel. Brent crude, the international standard, rose 63 cents to $84.40 a barrel.

A day earlier, it had dropped after U.S. President Donald Trump said over the weekend that he decided to hold off on new strikes against Iran at the urging of allies in the region.

Brent’s price careened between $72 and $102 last month as worries rose and fell over the war in Iran and when oil tankers would be allowed to freely exit the Persian Gulf again to deliver crude to customers worldwide.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury sank to 4.68% from 4.75% late Friday. It remains well above its 3.97% level from before the war with Iran.

New York can’t ban federal agents from wearing face coverings or require that they wear visible identification, a federal judge ruled Monday.

The ruling comes after a federal judge earlier this year blocked a similar law in California that was enacted after the Trump administration aggressively worked to increase immigration arrests.

For the Northern District of New York, U.S. District Judge Mae D’Agostino wrote that while New York "appears to be well-intentioned in its pursuit of transparent policing," that's not what the court is deciding.

“The issue now before the Court is about constitutionality—not transparency or preferable policy decisions,” she wrote.

The federal government has shown a likelihood that the measures go against the supremacy clause of the U.S. Constitution, which bars state governments from regulating federal law enforcement, D’Agostino wrote.

The measures were included in a slate of law enforcement policies as part of the state budget bill that was signed into law by Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul in May.

Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James said in a statement following the judge's decision that they "stand firm in our belief that masked agents do not make New York safer and our offices are reviewing all legal options at this time.”

New York's face coverings and identification measures took effect in June, according to the ruling.

California became the first state to ban most law enforcement officers from wearing facial coverings under a bill that was signed in September following a summer of high-profile raids by immigration officers in Los Angeles.

When the law was blocked, the decision was expected to have implications nationwide for other states that have pursued their own measures to place restrictions on immigration agents.

In May, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a federal lawsuit against Connecticut over a new state law that prohibits federal agents from wearing masks.

Ariana Grande will soon take a break from public life amid the ongoing discourse surrounding her health and body, her representative said Sunday.

Grande will be “taking a step back from visibility” following the completion of her Eternal Sunshine tour in London on September 1, the representative announced.

“She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” they told People magazine.

“This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.”

Grande will also no longer appear in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George, People has confirmed.

open image in gallery Ariana Grande has faced intense scrutiny about her health and body in recent years ( Getty )

open image in gallery The news of her withdrawal from public life comes just days after the release of her eighth studio album, petal ( AP )

The production was set to open at London's Barbican Centre next summer, with Grande due to star opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey.

A source close to Grande told People that she “cannot wait to support the brilliant team bringing this project to life.”

The news of Grande’s break from the public eye comes days after the release of her eighth studio album, Petal, which reignited the discourse surrounding her body and health.

British model, author and body positivity activist Charlotte Howard was among those to speak out following the release of Grande’s music video for “Petal” (the single of the same name from the new album) on July 31.

“I think it’s vital we discuss imagery/videos/content like these and the damage they can - and will - have on women and girls. WHAT YOU SEE HERE IS NOT NORMAL,” wrote Howard alongside stills from the music video.

“Over the past few weeks, as images of Ariana’s concert get plastered around online, I obviously see comments from worried fans, but I also see other people convincing others that she looks ‘healthy’, or that she has simply ‘lost puppy fat’. Some even make jokes about it.

“What I see is someone in desperate need of hospitalisation and care, and while I know it’s often impossible to help someone at this stage of anorexia, there HAS to be an immediate intervention.

“... I think it is absolutely appalling, from both a moral and capitalistic standpoint, to have released these videos and an album when this person needs psychiatric help and hospitalisation. The teams involved should be absolutely ashamed. ... I truly, truly hope she gets the help that she so desperately needs.”

Late last year, during the Wicked: For Good press tour, Grande issued a “loving reminder” to her fans and others to think before they speak.

On her Instagram Story, she reshared her 2024 interview with French internet personality Sally Poumbga, in which she was asked about beauty standards.

“I’ve been a specimen in a petri-dish since I was 17, so I’ve heard it all,” Grande said. “I’ve heard ‘what’s wrong’ with me, and then you fix it, and then it’s wrong for different reasons.

“I think in today’s society there’s a comfortability that we shouldn’t have, at all, commenting on others’ looks, appearance… what they think is going on ‘behind the scenes’ or health or how they present themselves,” she explained. “I think it’s dangerous, for both parties involved.”

Japan needs to adapt to the new methods of warfare like drones and artificial intelligence used in Ukraine and the Middle East and strengthen its defense industry, the government said Tuesday.

Japan has bolstered its military capability and spending in recent years and has started deploying long-range cruise missiles as a deterrence to China's military activity.

The 598-page defense paper adopted by the Cabinet on Tuesday reiterated that China is Japan’s biggest strategic challenge. Japan is alarmed by the growing presence and frequency of Chinese warships in the Pacific Ocean.

Combat drones for new warfare

Inspired by the use of drones by Ukraine, Japan considers it is essential to adapt to “new ways of warfare,” the paper said.

With many countries racing to develop combat drones, Japan's government prioritizes development of its own for a coastal defense, in combination with long-range missiles.

“Speed is key,” Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in early July.

The Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency recently selected four drone makers out of 38 applicants for a rapid development program and that they will advance to testing by Japan's navy in early August before a final selection.

A number of companies are developing similar drones. Toshiba announced Friday plans to jointly develop combat drones with startup Pro Drone.

Uncrewed weapons could help Japan make up for its decreasing number of service members in a country with a shrinking population.

Experts say developing fully homemade drones while Japan’s commercial drone market is dominated by Chinese imports would be a challenge.

Alarmed by China’s activity in the Pacific, Russia and North Korea

Japan has strengthened its military forces on southwestern islands in recent years and has started deploying long-range cruise missiles, as it worries about a conflict in Taiwan, which China claims as its territory.

The paper noted the growing presence Chinese warships and frequency of their activity in the Pacific as a major concern. The Defense Ministry has established a unit dedicated to study Japan’s Pacific strategy and strengthen its defense against China.

China has consistently increased its military spending without transparency and strengthened nuclear and missile capability extensively and rapidly, the defense paper said.

It noted that in last December Chinese aircraft locked their radars, considered possible preparation for firing missiles, on Japanese planes during Chinese aircraft carrier drills near southwestern Japan.

Two Chinese aircraft carriers were spotted last June near the southern Japanese island of Iwo Jima for the first time. This triggered Tokyo's worries about Beijing’s rapidly expanding military activity far beyond its borders and in disputed areas in the East China Sea.

Tensions between Tokyo and Beijing have escalated since Takaichi said in November that Chinese military action against Taiwan could justify Japan’s use of force.

China’s growing joint military operation with Russia around Japan, including joint bomber flights and warship operations, is also “a grave national security concern,” the paper said.

It says North Korea’s rapid development of missiles, including hypersonic arsenals, is an “increasingly serious and pressing threat” and that the North’s growing military ties with Russia and its backing for Moscow's war in Ukraine are a grave concern.

Bolstering defense industry, weapons sale

Strengthening arms production and technology is essential to Japan's military power, the paper said. The government has been expanding funding for startups and scientific research.

In a country that had maintained a pacifist pledge since the end of World War II, many established companies avoid ties to lethal weapons, but a growing number of startups are showing interest in converting dual-use technology for military use, officials say.

Japan’s recent scrapping of lethal weapons export ban could also help strengthen the country's underdeveloped defense industry.

Weapons technology transfer and joint development and production strengthens both Japanese defense industry base and Japan's ties with its defense partners, said Koizumi, whose travels to other countries have involved arms sales.

Japan recently made major deals, including the joint development and transfer of 11 upgraded Mogami-class frigates to Australia. It is discussing a similar deal with New Zealand and has struck a deal to sell retired destroyers to the Philippines.

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Sports.title: Champions League stadium to look unrecognisable as £171m renovation of 54,732-seater arena is approved
Sports.content:
NAPOLI are set to give the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona a mega-money makeover.

The Serie A giants, who are eyeing a summer move for Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile, have had major redevelopment plans approved.



It comes after Chelsea fans highlighted safety issues when they headed to Napoli in the Champions League last season.

And the Italian heavyweights’ 54,732-seater home will look unrecognisable after the £171million renovation is complete.



The athletics track separating the action from the raucous fans is set to be ditched as part of the proposal.

Napoli, who bagged their fourth Serie A crown last year, also want to extend the second tier and have the seating just seven metres from the edge of the pitch.



The third tier will also be reopened after being off limits to supporters due to safety concerns.

Structural vibrations could be felt when fans were celebrating, leading to changes needing to be made.

But having fans back in those areas could allow the capacity at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona – which was renamed in honour of the Argentine legend in 2020 – to increase to in the region of 65,000.

Initial preparatory work has already begun and is expected to move into a more advanced stage in the autumn.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Napoli, fresh from seeing Antonio Conte quit as their boss at the end of last term, are desperate not to stray too far from how the arena looked when it first opened in 1959.

The eye-catching renovation, which includes new VIP boxes and hospitality areas, is on course to take place in stages.

It means Napoli, who are preparing for another season of Champions League action, will not have to leave their home while upgrades are made.

And the project was given the green light after a proposal was submitted by Mayor Gaetano Manfredi and infrastructure councillor Edoardo Cosenza.



The majority of the building work is expected to get underway after Italian host cities for Euro 2032 have been selected.

But city and regional authorities insist Stadio Diego Armando Maradona will be revamped even if it is not in line to stage showdowns during the tournament.

Sports.title: Leeds boss Daniel Farke fumes as team are denied trophy after pre-season win over Liverpool
Sports.content:
DANIEL FARKE was left miffed that Leeds’ pre-season victory over Liverpool did not come with a trophy.

The Yorkshire club rounded off their US tour with a 4-2 win over the Reds in Chicago thanks to an excellent second-half comeback.



It made it two wins from three games after beating Sunderland and losing to Wrexham in the round-robin tournament.

A Dominic Calvert-Lewin double, plus goals from Brenden Aaronson and Sean Longstaff did the damage.



It meant Leeds finished as the top British club — but did not receive any silverware for their efforts.

And boss Farke said: “We won this tournament and actually I want the trophy.



Especially in the US, you normally get the trophy for everything!

“I am a bit annoyed, but all jokes aside, there couldn’t be a better ending of this tour.

“The boys have worked so hard — three weeks right now without a day off, more or less two weeks here in the US.

“Against Liverpool, we had more shots, more shots on target, way more corner kicks, set-pieces.

“We really fully deserved to win this game.

“Especially for such a brilliant, brilliant second half — so all credit goes to the players.

The Whites host German club RB Leipzig in their next pre-season friendly on Saturday.

Sports.title: Why Jude Bellingham nemesis Valentin Barco won’t care less if he gets booed at Premier League grounds with Chelsea
Sports.content:
ARGENTINIAN hothead Valentin Barco can expect a hostile reception from English fans whenever he plays for Chelsea this season.

But the red-haired firebrand who earned a clip round the ear from Jude Bellingham for his World Cup semi-final antics is no stranger to bouncing back from controversy.



Barco, 22, may have compatriot and fellow wind-up merchant Enzo Fernandez to help him run the gauntlet.

No-one has yet stumped up the £120m fee which Chelsea are demanding for Fernandez, who cupped his ears in front of Three Lions fans as he celebrated his equaliser against Thomas Tuchel’s men.





Yet whatever happens with his international team-mate, Barco will surely face the consequences of his behaviour following Lautaro Martinez’s stoppage-time winner.

The former Brighton star, who was an unused substitute, ran on to the pitch and appeared to taunt England players.

And after the final whistle, Barco said or did something to antagonise Bellingham further, which resulted in the slap for which the Three Lions star has escaped punishment.

Venezuela’s Bryant Ortega was not so lucky when Barco was up to no good in an Olympic qualifying match back in February 2024.



After Barco was penalised for a foul, he threw the ball at another opponent, Rafael Uzcategui, catching him on the head.

Ortega retaliated on behalf of his team-mate in similar fashion, and both he and Barco were sent off.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Argentina feared Barco would be banned for the remaining two matches of the final stage of qualifying..

But Barco received just a one-game ban and returned for the decisive game against Brazil.

Playing at left back, he secured his third assist of the campaign by setting up what turned out to be the only goal of the game, which sent Argentina to the Paris 2024 games.



But for good measure, Barco showed the other side of his game in stoppage time by earning a yellow card for kicking the ball away as Brazil prepared to take a free kick.

All this happened after Barco had signed for Brighton from Boca Juniors in January 2024 for just under £8m – but before he made an appearance for the Seagulls.

The transatlantic move was not the first time Barco had gone the extra mile to advance his career.

Boca spotted his talent at an early age, but his home in Veinticinco de Mayo was a long way from the academy.

Barco revealed: “When I started playing football, my mother and then my father would travel 100km to take me to training every day.



“After that, we moved to live next to the stadium.”

Boca, where Diego Maradona and many other Argentina legends rose to fame, converted Barco from a wide forward into a left-sided defender.

He made his debut at the age of 16 and at 19 was part of the team which made it all the way to the 2023 final of the Copa Libertadores, South America’s equivalent of the Champions League.

In the last 16 clash with Uruguay’s Nacional, he stepped up to score the fifth and decisive penalty in the shootout.

Barco started the final against Brazilian side Fluminense, but Boca lost 2-1 after extra time.



Manchester City were among the clubs monitoring Barco.

But it was Brighton who announced Barco was following in the footsteps of fellow South American recruits to the Amex such as fellow Argentinian Alexis Mac Allister and Ecuador’s Moises Caicedo, now his team-mate at Chelsea.

Barco made seven appearances for Brighton in the remainder of the 2023/4 campaign, including three starts in the Premier League.



The Seagulls sent the young man on loan to Spanish club Sevilla for the 2024/5 campaign.

But he returned in the New Year after struggling for game time and with injuries. Barco and fiancee Yaz Jaureguy, an influencer from Argentina, were also victims of a burglary.

A move to Strasbourg and the coaching of future Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior kickstarted Barco’s European adventure.

After recovering from a hamstring problem, he started all 14 remaining Ligue 1 games.

Just as significantly, Rosenior unlocked his potential in a new position.



Barco initially played as a wing back for Strasbourg, but soon found himself playing in the centre of midfield alongside Andrey Santos, who was on loan from sister club Chelsea.

He thrived at the heart of the team and became a key player in the side that secured Conference League qualification.

Barco was outstanding in a 4-2 win over Lyon in March 2025 and was given three days off by Rosenior to spend with Jaureguy and their new baby daughter.



Barco joined Strasbourg permanently for £8m and continued his development, even after Rosenior left in January to replace Enzo Maresca as Chelsea boss.

The Blues were immediately linked with a move to sign him, and personal terms were allegedly agreed back In April..

Strasbourg enjoyed another good season, reaching the semi finals of the Conference League and French Cup.

The only blot on Barco’s copybook was a red card for an X-rated foul on Lens’ Morgan Guilavogui last November.

Until the World Cup semi final.



Argentinians call people with ginger hair like Barco “Colo” – short for “colorado”.

And he lived up to their reputation for being combustible with his behaviour against England, despite not kicking a ball in anger in Atlanta.

Barco can expect plenty of stick up and down the country when he pulls on a Chelsea shirt following a move which even some Blues fans are criticising.

But like any good Argentinian, he is unlikely to care.

Sports.title: West Ham chief David Sullivan advised to stay away from home matches after ‘serious historic allegations’
Sports.content:
DAVID Sullivan, West Ham’s co-owner, has been advised to stay away from home matches following allegations of historic sexual misconduct.

The 77-year-old billionaire recently quit the football club after a BBC Panorama investigation revealed several women accused Sullivan of predatory behaviour and sexual exploitation, which he denies



The London Stadium, where West Ham play their home games, said it “recommended” Sullivan does not attend these matches, the BBC revealed.

The advice was given following concerns about “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.



A spokesperson for the stadium told the BBC it asked Sullivan to give advance notice if he planned to make a visit so additional safety measures could be implemented.

It said: “Following media reports at the end of the season regarding a safeguarding matter being managed by the club, London Stadium sought further information to ensure it could fulfil its own safeguarding responsibilities.”



The stadium also said that West Ham informed it that “the matter was investigated and that the club does not consider there to be an ongoing safeguarding risk associated with Mr Sullivan attending the stadium”.

Sullivan has branded the claims of serious sexual misconduct as “factually incorrect and entirely false”.



Despite this, the stadium still wanted Sullivan to stay away from home games following fan unrest.

However, it is understood that Sullivan is expected to defy these requests.

The BBC approached Sullivan for comment but he did not respond.

The Sun have approached London Stadium and West Ham for comment.

This new advice comes after a BBC Panorama and Times investigation revealed allegations against Sullivan for historical sex abuse.



He has been accused of abusing his power to prey on young women for sex – allegations dating back to the 1980s.

Women alleged he used his position as owner of the Daily and Sunday Sport to pressure aspiring models into sex and proposition others.

One woman, known as Florence, claimed she felt forced to have sex with him at his Essex mansion.

She said she made excuses – telling him her boyfriend was in the house and that she was on her period – but claims Sullivan ignored her.

Sullivan disputes her version of events and says her account of his home makes her claims implausible.



The tycoon had also been secretly banned from having contact with the club’s youth and women’s matches for three years over safeguarding fears.

A safeguarding panel made up of the club, the FA and the local authority ruled he should be kept away from the teams and was informed of the ban in writing by a senior club executive.

Sullivan, who had been on the board for more than 16 years, later resigned and vowed to sue the BBC for libel, calling the Panorama allegations made against him “defamatory”.

Following his resignation in June, a Hammers club statement read: “West Ham United can confirm that Joint-Chair David Sullivan has stepped down from his position with immediate effect.

“Mr Sullivan has also resigned as a director of both WH Holding Limited and West Ham United Football Club, having been made aware of the impending publication of serious historic allegations.



“It is understood none of the allegations relate to West Ham United or any of its operations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Through his own legal representatives Mr Sullivan denies any illegal conduct and has taken the decision to step down in order to avoid disruption to the Club while he addresses the matter privately.

“Interim Chief Executive Officer Karim Virani, reporting into the current Board of Directors, will continue to be responsible for leading the Club’s day-to-day operations.”

Sports.title: Man Utd paying price for years of transfer failure as Marcus Rashford and £36.5m flop prove impossible to budge
Sports.content:
THE 2007 transfer window was Manchester United’s best — not just for who they bought, but also for who they sold.

It is in stark contrast to the current summer, where the Red Devils’ only senior sale agreed has been 21-year-old Tyler Fredricson.



The full-back made four appearances before moving to the Ineos-owned Lausanne Sport in Switzerland — so he barely counts.

While United’s Big Six rivals are splashing the cash, the Red Devils are paying the price for years of a sub-par approach to sales.



Arsenal, hot in the pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr, are the only one of those clubs to have splashed less cash than the Old Trafford outfit.

The Red Devils have so far spent just £87million on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Tynan Thompson, while keeper Karl Darlow has arrived on a free.



Put simply, the more cash that United generate from outgoings, the more they can spend — and the lack of sales are hurting them.

Manchester City and Chelsea regularly lean on their network of sister clubs to trade players for profit.

That could be a homegrown academy product sold, for example, from Chelsea to Strasbourg.

Or a BlueCo-owned player going the other way before getting flipped within 18 months for a profit on the Stamford Bridge books.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Ineos also own Nice — but United have not taken advantage of that relationship, with Sir Jim Ratcliffe looking to sell the French-owned club. While hardly fetching mega sums, United’s academy still sells.

Andreas Pereira (£10m), James Garner (£15m), Dean Henderson (£20m), Anthony Elanga (£15m) and Alejandro Garnacho (£40m) all moved to Premier League rivals since 2022.

But Kobbie Mainoo and Shea Lacey are the only current first-team players produced by United’s academy.

Garnacho was the last United graduate to generate serious profit when Chelsea brought him last summer.

Nineteen years ago, United were pulling in good money for players they wanted to sell. In the same summer they signed Nani, Anderson and Owen Hargreaves.



Kieran Richardson joined Sunderland for £5.5m, while fellow academy graduate Giuseppe Rossi relocated to Villarreal permanently for £6.7m.

Alan Smith went to Newcastle for £6million and Gabriel Heinze headed to Real Madrid for £8m, having failed to engineer a move to bitter rivals Liverpool.

United were in a position of strength as reigning Prem champions.



And it helped that playing for Sir Alex Ferguson increased a player’s valuation.

Roy Keane could barely stomach sharing the same oxygen as Ferguson after United dumped him — but still signed five players from his old club as Sunderland boss.

It is incredible that Garnacho, Scott McTominay, Rasmus Hojlund, Mason Greenwood, Daniel James, David Beckham, Cristiano Ronaldo, Angel Di Maria and Romelu Lukaku are the only players United have sold for £25m or more.

The Red Devils desperately trumpeted Garnacho to Chelsea as a record academy sale at £40m.

He appeared to be sold on the cheap but Garnacho, now at Aston Villa, was so feckless that Chelsea might even have overpaid.



Out-of-favour forward Joshua Zirkzee is still on United’s books and Marcus Rashford remains in the building after a permanent move to Barcelona fell through following his loan.

It has been so long since Rashford was last back in the fold at United that he has not set foot in their new £50m building at Carrington, reopened a year ago.

It is a blow for Rashford that Villa, his ex-club who he thanked for his England World Cup 2026 call-up, opted for Garnacho, his old United left-wing challenger.

Rashford is not exactly old at 28 — but Villa and Barca moved for younger wingers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His £325,000 weekly salary makes a sale prohibitive.



Even Richardson, a very different left winger at Old Trafford 20 years ago, was an easier sell.

Sports.title: West Ham eye transfer for forgotten Tottenham star, 27, who hasn’t played for the club in three years
Sports.content:
WEST HAM are interested in signing Tottenham forward Manor Solomon.

The Israel star, 27, is set to leave Spurs this summer and talks over an exit will ramp up this week – with Fiorentina, where he spent the second half of last season, also keen.



The Hammers are looking for reinforcements out wide following Crysencio Summerville’s exit.

Super agent Pini Zahavi is involved in talks and wants to find Solomon a new home before the season gets underway.



Fiorentina are pushing to bring the winger back after he helped the Serie A side qualify for Europe last season.

Solomon’s spell at Fiorentina in the second half of last season was his third loan spell in two years – after also spending time with Leeds and Villarreal.

He enjoyed a box office campaign at Leeds and helped Daniel Farke’s side win promotion back to the top-flight.

A return to the Prem is also an attractive option for the versatile winger, who can play on either flank.

He joined Tottenham from Fulham in 2023 but has played just SIX competitive games.

His last outing for Tottenham came back in September 2023 under Ange Postecoglou.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Despite his uncertain future, Solomon has featured regularly in pre-season, starting friendlies against MK Dons, Auckland FC, Sydney FC and Chelsea.

Only midfielder Archie Gray has clocked more minutes than the 49-cap Israel international.

But while Roberto De Zerbi has taken a long look at the winger this summer, he is still expected to leave before the transfer window shuts.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes confirms he’s joined up with Newcastle as Brazil star posts update amid Arsenal transfer battle
Sports.content:
BRUNO GUIMARAES has confirmed that he has joined up with Newcastle despite Arsenal pursuing his signature.

The Brazilian midfielder is one of the Gunners’ top targets this summer ahead of their Premier League title defence.



Guimaraes, 28, has touched down in Spain to reunite with his Newcastle team-mates.

The midfielder shared a picture on Instagram of the club’s hotel in La Manga.



He is a late arrival for the Magpies’ pre-season due to his commitments at the World Cup with the Selecao.

Arsenal have finally made a formal offer for the star but it has been rebuffed.

SunSport understands the expectation is that Guimaraes will get his wish and move to the Emirates before the end of the transfer window.

Talks have been taking place through intermediaries for weeks, and it is thought Newcastle are holding out for around £80million.

The Samba ace was expected to meet with new boss Matthias Jaissle and sporting director Ross Wilson in La Manga.

Guimaraes, however, has his heart set on joining Arsenal and following Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali out the door.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Gunners just need to finalise a fee for the midfielder, as personal terms will not be an issue.

Back on Tyneside, all references to Guimaraes appear to have been removed from St James’ Park.

Banners showing the star posing in the club’s new kit have reportedly been replaced by banners with other stars, per The Mag.

Arsenal are also chasing Guimaraes’ Brazil team-mate, Vinicius Junior.

The electric winger was all smiles as he returned to Real Madrid ahead of crunch talks over his future.



He has entered the final year of his eye-watering £400,000-a-week Bernabeu deal.

The transfer for Vinicius will be far more challenging and hinges on whether he turns down the chance to stay at Real Madrid.

The Spanish giants have been trying to tie him down for over a year, but no agreement has been found.



Arsenal are waiting in the wings and believe they can offer an attractive package, if Vinicius refuses to sign an extension in the Spanish capital.

Mikel Arteta was bullish on the club’s transfer plans after their 4-1 win over Girona last Saturday.

The Gunners boss said: “We are already active and trying to improve on and evolve the team. That is clear.

“We expect to have movements in the next few weeks. Obviously we want to get better like anyone else and you can see the transfer market, and our opponents, what we are doing.

“We won’t sit still and we are very ambitious with where we want to go.”



Arsenal have already signed a left winger this summer, splashing out £34million on Club Brugge winger Christos Tzolis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Greek star, who scored in the win over Girona, is ready to fight for his place and not worried by Arsenal target Vinicius.

Tzolis said: “Obviously I’m confident as a player, so I don’t think about the future and what the club will do in this position.”

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option as club stance on striker emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option as club stance on striker emerges

Manchester United continue to be linked with multiple deals during the transfer window as Marcus Rashford reportedly attracts attention from a new club

View 2 Images Manchester United star Marcus Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester United are nearing the start of the new season as the transfer window rumbles on. Michael Carrick’s side have brought in several new signings as the manager looks to improve his squad.

‌



Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have been at the centre of United’s midfield rebuild following Casemiro’s departure to Inter Miami. Experienced goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived at Old Trafford, alongside young shot-stopper Kit Margetson and attacking prospect Tynan Thompson.

‌



United have been linked with moves for several targets, including Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly and Newcastle full-back Lewis Hall. However, Marcus Rashford's future remains a topic of discussion after Barcelona’s decision not to sign the forward permanently.

‌



Meanwhile, United striker Benjamin Sesko is also claimed to have attracted interest from Bayern Munich. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding the club.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Marcus Rashford given fresh transfer option

Turkish giants Fenerbahce have reportedly made contact over a possible move for Marcus Rashford. The 28-year-old faces an uncertain future at United after Barcelona opted not to trigger their £26million buy option at the end of his loan spell.

‌



Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

Alejandro Garnacho takes brutal swipe at Chelsea immediately after Aston Villa debut READ MORE :

The Sun reports that Fenerbahce are prepared to “break the bank” for Rashford if the England international is prepared to join the club. It is claimed that the forward is one of three players on a shortlist, which also includes Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr and AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

It is reported that Fernerbahce have made contact with Rashford’s representatives to gauge his interest in joining the club. Rashford scored and assisted 14 goals apiece for Barcelona last season but the Catalan side decided to sign forwards Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi this summer.

"What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. "Sometimes it's not always that you do know what happens with players who are on loan. I think our situation is not easy for that.

‌



"But I appreciate working with him a lot; he's a fantastic player and a fantastic person. I think also the team miss him, I will miss him, but it's life, this is what we have to accept."

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has been linked with Bayern Munich (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Bayern Munich stance on Benjamin Sesko emerges

Bayern Munich reportedly remain interested in United striker Benjamin Sesko. The German side have previously considered a move for the forward and still view the 23-year-old as potentially part of the club’s long-term transfer plans.

‌



CFBayern Insider reports that Sesko continues to be a “very interesting” option for the club. Harry Kane currently leads the line for Bayern but it is claimed that the England captain could occupy a deeper role in the future, leaving space for another centre forward in the team.

Bayern have signed Ismael Saibari from PSV Eindhoven, reducing the need for another new striker. However, the report adds that Sesko remains on Bayern’s list of options. Sesko ended his debut season at United by scoring seven goals in 13 games under Carrick.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Next Bruno Guimaraes bid imminent as Mikel Arteta message to target emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Next Bruno Guimaraes bid imminent as Mikel Arteta message to target emerges

Arsenal are pushing hard to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle

View 2 Images Arsenal have reportedly had a bid for Bruno Guimaraes rejected (Image: Getty )

After a slow and somewhat disappointing first half of the summer transfer window, Arsenal are ramping up their pursuit of several key targets. Since the Gunners’ Champions League final defeat to PSG in May, Mikel Arteta has repeatedly stressed the need to add quality signings, especially in forward positions.

‌



The Premier League champions’ underwhelming early business included announcing Piero Hincapie’s permanent move and signing third-choice goalkeeper Illan Meslier. They followed that up by replacing the recently-departed Leandro Trossard with £34million Greek winger Christos Tzolis, who grabbed a goal on his debut against Girona last Saturday.

‌



Arsenal’s first game of the 2026/27 campaign - a Community Shield clash with Manchester City on August 16 - will soon be in view as the season draws closer. As such, sporting director Andrea Berta is expected to push hard in the coming days to bring in a defender, a midfielder and a forward - which Arsenal hope will be Vinicius Junior.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer stories involving the Gunners.

Arsenal receive immediate response after finally submitting first Bruno Guimaraes offer READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting READ MORE :

Second Bruno Guimaraes bid looms

Several reports claim that Newcastle United have rejected Arsenal’s first official offer for Bruno Guimaraes. The Gunners’ opening bid fell short of the £80m valuation the Magpies have placed on their captain and star midfielder.

‌



However, Arsenal are expected to return with an improved offer for the 28-year-old, whose contract expires in June 2028. Guimaraes has emerged as Arteta’s most pressing target in recent weeks and has reportedly already agreed personal terms with the north Londoners.

The Brazilian has also made Newcastle aware of his desire to leave, with the Emirates Stadium said to be his favoured destination. It is understood that Guimaraes is not willing to force an exit, however. Arsenal had floated a £45m verbal offer at the start of the transfer window but they were immediately shut down by the Magpies.

Arteta’s private message to target

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is pushing to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: Getty )

‌



Arteta has reportedly taken charge of Arsenal’s pursuit of Vinicius by directly speaking to the Brazilian winger on the phone. The Gunners boss, according to Spanish outlet AS, has told Vinicius he will base the entire Arsenal project around the 26-year-old, should he join this summer.

It emerged last month that all key personnel at Arsenal had decided to pursue the Real Madrid forward, sanctioning the move in spite of the enormous cost of getting a deal over the line. Despite Vinicius’ contract expiring next summer, a fee of around £130m has been mooted in order to convince Los Blancos to part ways with the two-time Champions League winner.

Real Madrid remain determined to keep Vinicius but will look to sell him if he refuses to agree to a contract extension. They are reportedly unwilling to adjust their most recent contract offer to Vinicius and the club believes the decision now lies with the player.

It has previously been said that Vinicius is not in a rush to renew his deal, but new boss Jose Mourinho was prepared to step in in order to keep his star players.

Sports.title: Donald Trump 'will do everything he can' to save Gianni Infantino's job as FIFA president
Sports.content:
Donald Trump 'will do everything he can' to save Gianni Infantino's job as FIFA president

The US President will reportedly do 'everything he can' to save his close friend Gianni Infantino's job after calls for him to go following his plan to sell stakes of FIFA

View 3 Images Trump to do 'everything he can' to save Gianni Infantino's job (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Donald Trump 'will do everything he can' to save Gianni Infantino's job as FIFA president, according to insiders.

‌



Infantino's job is under threat after his plan to sell off a stake in a new FIFA organisation sparked furious backlash.

‌



The scheme has been abandoned after the backlash, with many teams saying they would boycott the World Cup if it were to go ahead.

‌



However, according to a senior administration official close to the pair the president is very fond of Infantino after he helped the US host the “best World Cup ever” and will support his bid to remain as FIFA chief, despite calls for him to go.

View 3 Images The pair's relationship has been questioned several times (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Infantino's relationship with Trump has been regularly questioned, especially after the recent World Cup.

‌



During this year's tournament, co-hosted by the US, Trump said he phoned the FIFA chief to complain after a red card was given to the USA's star striker.

His one-match ban was then suspended, sparking debates about political interference in the game.

“Gianni helped us a lot to deliver the best World Cup ever. The president likes him a lot.

‌



"I am sure the president will do everything possible to help him,” the source told The Telegraph.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

“I don’t think the president will change his mind on him, because he is a loyal person. Gianni really delivered the World Cup for the United States. We value that.”

‌



Others have claimed that the relationship between the pair has gone too far.

David Davies, who held several senior roles at the FA between 1994 and 2006 said: "My instinct is that it's gone too far. What's happening has gone too far for him."

He added that Infantino is a "political-style" FIFA boss, who had been "seduced for too long" by Donald Trump.

‌



Despite reports that Trump will support Infantino as his job is on the line, in the UK, the FIFA president does not have the same backing from political leaders.

Andy Burnham has repeated his belief that Infantino is "not the right man to lead football" and urges him to stand down from his role.

It is understood that the English FA are preparing a letter withdrawing its support for Infantino's re-election, following the Welsh FA.

Article continues below

Despite these withdrawals, there are currently no other candidates that have declared to challenge him.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson's ex-assistant at Man Utd joins his son in new League One role
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson's ex-assistant at Man Utd joins his son in new League One role

Rene Meulensteen has taken on a senior role with Stockport County as the League One club bring in the man who previously served as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United

View 2 Images Rene Meulensteen has taken on a role at Stockport County (Image: @StockportCounty)

Sir Alex Ferguson's former assistant at Manchester United, Rene Meulensteen, has landed a shock role at Stockport County.

‌



The Dutchman, who also served as Fulham's manager for a brief period, has been appointed at Edgeley Park taking on the role of director of football methodology.

‌



Stockport finished third in League One last season but lost out in the play-off final at Wembley. They've turned to Meulensteen for some top-flight experience and his new role will see him work closely with Stockport’s first-team staff, which will also allow him to collaborate with his son Joppe, who is a coach at the club.

‌



His remit will also involve a part in developing the football programme across both the academy and first team. The club's sporting director, Damien Allen, said: "Today marks a significant milestone in our club's history with the appointment of our first-ever director of football methodology.

Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal saga has Newcastle in contention for all-time worst transfer window READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss READ MORE :

"This landmark appointment reflects our commitment to building an elite football department, where every player and coach across the club is aligned behind a clear football philosophy, coaching methodology, identity and way of working.

‌



"From the outset, we were determined to appoint someone with an exceptional track record of developing players. Throughout his distinguished career, he has played a key role in maximising the potential of world-class players, including Cristiano Ronaldo, and was an integral member of one of the most successful coaching teams in modern football, winning 11 major honours, including four Premier League titles and the UEFA Champions League."

Meulensteen spent 12 years working at Old Trafford across two different spells. His first stint on the red side of Manchester was from 2001 and 2006. After a year out, he was back alongside Ferguson from 2007 to 2013.

View 2 Images Rene Meulensteen worked as a long-time assistant to Sir Alex Ferguson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Whilst at Old Trafford he helped the Red Devils win multiple Premier League titles and was also present when they claimed the Champions League in 2008. He left the club after the Scot's retirement.

Meulensteen heads to Stockport off the back of a World Cup campaign that saw him working as the assistant coach for Iraq, who went out in the group stages. His managerial career has also seen him work at Russian club Anzhi Makhachkala, where he managed under European Cup winner Guus Hiddink.
