In the 2018-19 season, Como were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football, after going bankrupt twice in the previous 15 years. Last season, the small northern Italian club finished fourth after an extraordinary campaign, producing a series of outstanding performances that surprised the football world.

Sports.title: Worn in the USA: Liverpool’s pre-season tour had highs but exposed glaring gaps in the squad | Andy Hunter
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola’s first pre-season tour as the Liverpool head coach produced wins over Sunderland in Nashville and Wrexham in New York before ending in a 4-2 defeat against Leeds in Chicago. The Guardian followed the tour throughout and here are a few things we learned.

Iraola’s vision will take time

Liverpool’s second-half display against Leeds was both concerning and valuable for the Iraola as set-piece problems and a tendency to switch off – two of last season’s recurring themes – reared their ugly head again, albeit after he had made changes. Liverpool’s opening 45 minutes, however, was their best of the tour and showed how effective his front-foot, more intense style can be with the big names back. But that process is only just under way.

Iraola is yet to even meet Virgil van Dijk, Cody Gakpo, Alisson, Alexis Mac Allister and new signing Víctor Muñoz since his appointment almost two months ago, never mind coach them. They will be finally acquainted when the squad reports back for training on Wednesday, having been given a little time off to recover from Sunday night’s flight from Chicago. Mac Allister will be still absent after his World Cup exertions. There is less than three weeks to go and only two more friendlies (although it is a double-header against Como at Anfield) before Liverpool open their Premier League season at Newcastle. “I would like to say on the first day we are going to be perfect, everyone will be in place,” Iraola said. “But probably it is not going to be like this.”

Head coach needs more backing

For most of the tour, Iraola was without eight first-team players due to World-Cup holidays and six because of injury, either recovering from or, as in the unfortunate Joe Gomez’s case, sustained in the US. No prizes for stating that Liverpool’s performances and adaptation to Iraola’s methods would have been much more advanced with 14 extra first-team players available. Even so, glaring gaps remain in the team when every option is taken into account.

View image in fullscreen Liverpool knew about Mohamed Salah’s departure months ago, but have yet to line up a replacement. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Mohamed Salah’s departure was announced in March. Talks to end his contract one year early commenced earlier. Five months on from the announcement, he is yet to be replaced. The seriousness of Conor Bradley’s knee injury means Liverpool remain light at right-back. There are the highest hopes for Jérémy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni – the latter has transformed himself into a strapping Adonis while recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury, by the way – while 18-year-olds Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Mor Talla Ndiaye did well in the US. But Liverpool are lacking Premier League experience in central defence and Ndukwe will be unable to play this season due to post-Brexit work permit difficulties. Gomez’s injury record means he must be considered a bonus when fit, rather than one of four options. It was interesting to hear Iraola explain how he likes wingers to play both flanks, and the advantages of switching them during a game, but Liverpool’s right side could be a problem even if they succeed in signing Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

View image in fullscreen Trey Nyoni’s confident and assured displays pressed his case for more Liverpool game time. Photograph: Kamil Krzaczyński/AFP/Getty Images

Nyoni is now firmly in Iraola’s plans

There was an enforced reliance on young players during the tour and Iraola was genuinely impressed by the levels many showed in training and the friendlies. Ndukwe and Talla Ndiaye, as mentioned, Lewis Koumas, Kieran Morrison and Luke Chambers were among them. But no prospect pushed their first team claims further than Trey Nyoni, who grew in stature and confidence with every outing. The 19-year-old and Rio Ngumoha were permanent fixtures in Arne Slot’s squad last season, but while the winger made 19 appearances in the Premier League, including five starts, Nyoni had to settle for six league outings from the bench. On this evidence, there will be many more this season. The midfielder looked immediately at ease with Iraola’s instructions to find forward options as quickly as possible and did so whether under pressure or by creating space for himself with intelligent movement. His pass in the buildup to Florian Wirtz’s goal against Leeds was exquisite and in keeping with his contribution overall. Nyoni said after the Leeds game he knew he had to improve this summer. He was as good as his word.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Jones did not seize chance

To pinch a phrase from Salah, Curtis Jones looked more out than in at times as he enters the final 12 months of his Liverpool contract with increasing interest from the Italian champions, Inter. Unlike Nyoni and Dominik Szoboszlai, the 25-year-old did not adapt comfortably to Iraola’s requirements for a central midfielder and particularly struggled when introduced in the second half against Leeds. But it was his petulant reaction to not receiving the captain’s armband from Szoboszlai against Wrexham that did him fewest favours.

Jones was also overlooked for the captaincy when Gomez exited the opening game against Sunderland. On both occasions the armband was passed to Kostas Tsimikas, a reserve left-back who spent last season on loan at Roma. Of course, that was going to annoy a boyhood Liverpool fan and one of the more senior players on the tour, and Jones, Szoboszlai and Tsimikas all went to great lengths to laugh off the incident in the days after the Wrexham win. The row might have been overblown on social media, but given Iraola stresses the importance of the collective, Jones’s individualistic behaviour jarred with what he is trying to build.

View image in fullscreen Dominik Szoboszlai led the way for Liverpool on the US tour. Photograph: Daniel Bartel/Getty Images

Szoboszlai wins popularity contest

In the absence of Salah, Andy Robertson, Van Dijk and Alisson, and in keeping with his status as Liverpool’s player of last season, Szoboszlai was undoubtedly the big attraction for fans in the US. The Hungary captain’s every introduction and contribution was met with fanatical acclaim and his was the face the media wanted on their channels. More importantly for Iraola, Szoboszlai led the way in training and his leadership was invaluable given the relative inexperience of the squad. Fresh from signing a new five-year contract, the 25-year-old is an obvious choice to fill one of the vice-captain vacancies created by the departures of Salah and Robertson.

Sports.title: ‘Doesn’t make sense’ – West Ham warned they’re making transfer ‘mistake’
Sports.content:
West Ham are making a 'mistake' by selling Freddie Potts, according to former Hammers star Kevin Nolan.

talkSPORT understands that Potts has been granted permission to travel to Belgium to undergo a medical ahead of a £10million move to Belgian side Club Brugge.



2 Potts, who has been with West Ham since he was six, is on the cusp of a £10m move to Belgian side Club Brugge Credit: Getty

The midfielder was expected to play a key role for West Ham in the coming Championship campaign as the Hammers seek an immediate Premier League return.

And yet, Potts is now set to leave the London Stadium, ending a 17-year association with the east London outfit.

Nolan, who spent four years on the West Ham books, revealed to Alex Crook on talkSPORT on Monday that he is 'surprised' that the capital side are cashing in on the 22-year-old.



"I think this probably could turn out to be a bit of a mistake, but it's good money for Freddie," Nolan said.

"I think it's a great move for Freddie to go to Club Brugge and be able to play in Europe, and play the style he wants.



"I'm quite surprised that this has been allowed to happen, if I'm honest.

"I thought that he could be one of the players who could stand up this year for West Ham.



"It doesn't make sense to me, but I wish Freddie all the luck because he's a great kid, lovely family, and I'm sure he'll go and be successful over there."

2 Potts' impending exit has caught a number of club legends off guard Credit: Getty

'I don't get it'

Nolan's comments on Potts echo Tony Cottee's words on the player's impending exit.

Former Hammers striker Cottee joined Jeff Stelling and Andy Townsend on talkSPORT Breakfast where he admitted his disappointment at seeing the 22-year-old go.



"I don't get it. Freddie Potts, I don't know I might be a bit biased," he said.

"I played with his dad and I want to see the academy players. I don't get it, £10million to Brugge, I think they're talking about.

"When he played in the Championship two seasons ago, he was Player of the Year for Portsmouth, he was the Player of the Year for Wycombe in League One and we're getting rid of a good young academy player.

"It doesn't make sense to me at all. Alright, £10million, you could argue that the club needs a bit of money to pay the bills.



"I get that at the moment, but in the grand scale of things, you've got to keep your good academy boys.

"West Ham might have raised well over £200million by the time the season starts.

"At which point, why are you selling an academy player for £10million? I don't get that one."

Sports.title: Inside the latest on Jack Grealish’s future as ‘fake reports’ dismissed
Sports.content:
Gabby Agbonlahor has hit out at 'fake reports' surrounding the reason Jack Grealish missed Manchester City's pre-season tour of Asia.

Grealish was a notable omission from the travelling squad, with rumours circulating he was left in England deliberately.

2 Grealish hasn't played since suffering a foot injury on loan at Everton Credit: instagram @jackgrealish

The City forward corrected one outlet's report that he and teammate Kalvin Phillips had been 'left out of' the selection that flew to the Far East.

"Just to let you know I’m still recovering from an injury so I’m not training yet. Haven’t been left out so stop talking poo poo thanks," Grealish wrote on an Instagram post.

And Agbonlahor has reinforced Grealish's claims as the pair discussed the latter's future while on holiday.

When asked about the possibility of returning to Aston Villa on Drive on Monday, Agbonlahor said: "I don't think so."

The talkSPORT pundit then elaborated: "I didn't have a conversation about Villa, I had a conversation about his future.

"There's been so many fake reports about how he wasn't called for the (pre-season) tour and he wasn't wanted, that's all nonsense.

"He's not able to train yet, so he's been out training at Real Mallorca's training ground, been putting the hard yards in, looking after himself, training hard.

"He just said he's hungry. If it's at Manchester City, if it's another club - I can't say which one it is - he wants to play football, he wants to get back."

The Greal Deal

Grealish spent last season on loan with Merseyside outfit Everton, and made a bright start to life at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Indeed, the 30-year-old managed two goals and six assists but his time under David Moyes was cut short due to a foot injury sustained against former side Villa back in January.

2 Grealish started brightly at Everton before a foot injury cut his time on Merseyside short Credit: Getty

A potential return to Everton was discussed on Drive, to which Agbonlahor, who had previously defended Grealish, said: "It could be an option, why not?

"David Moyes loves him, he knows the club, and there's talk about (Iliman) Ndiaye going to Saudi Arabia.

"I think whatever happens, whatever club he joins, if it's at Man City or he goes back to Everton, or another club, he's hungry.

"He's in his last year as well - in your last year, you need to be playing football, you need to be performing."

"Look, for instance, at Jadon Sancho now, it's a shame to see (him without a club), he's 26, I don't know who he's training with."

Agbonlahor's comments come after new City head coach Enzo Maresca previously admitted he is yet to speak with Grealish.

"I didn't speak with Jack while I am here. Jack is a City player. When we are back in Manchester, if he is fit he will work with us," the Italian said.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough vs Wrexham LIVE commentary: Kick-off time, team news and where to watch Carabao Cup tie for free
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough vs Wrexham LIVE commentary: Kick-off time, team news and where to watch Carabao Cup tie for free

The English domestic football season is finally back - and first up, it's the Carabao Cup that takes centre stage.

In an unusual change, the first round of the competition is being held before the EFL kickstarts their new campaign.



3 The first round of the Carabao Cup kicks off this week Credit: Getty

And in one of the opening games, Championship rivals Middlesbrough and Wrexham clash at the Riverside Stadium.

Boro just missed out on a place in the Premier League last season, losing in the play-off final to Hull City after being handed a place in the showpiece due to Southampton's Spygate scandal.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg will want to come out fighting again this term, and he'll be keen to get things going with a cup win.



As for Wrexham, they finished one place outside the play-offs and reached the fourth round of the Carabao Cup last season.

Phil Parkinson's side will hope to go deeper into the competition this time around as they eye another Hollywood story.



Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: talkSPORT coverage

This Carabao Cup first round tie will take place on Friday, August 7, with kick-off at the Riverside set for 8pm.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of the game from Mark Wilson and former Newcastle defender Steve Howey.



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



3 Wrexham reached the fourth round of the Carabao Cup last season Credit: Getty

The all-Championship clash will also be broadcast free-to-air on ITV, with the game also streamed online on ITVX.

Sky Sports will be broadcasting the action too.

Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: Team news

Middlesbrough will hope that star attacker Morgan Whittaker is available to feature amid interest from West Ham.

Meanwhile, new signings Sebastian Berhalter, Will Lankshear and Jeremy Sarmiento could all make their cup debuts.



Leo Castledine, a 21-year-old attacking midfielder, scored two in Boro's final friendly.

3 Whittaker is attracting interest from West Ham this summer Credit: Getty

In the Wrexham camp, Danny Imray could start his first competitive game for the club after making his debut in pre-season.

Kieffer Moore is likely to lead the line, with Sam Smith, Nathan Broadhead and Bailey Cadamarteri all available too.



Full-back Liberato Cacace missed a lot of football last term through injury, but he should be fit to now play regularly.

Middlesbrough vs Wrexham: Pre-season results

Middlesbrough drew their last pre-season game 3-3 against Espanyol, to end their preparations with a thriller.

They lost 3-1 to Huddersfield and drew 1-1 with Scottish champions Celtic in their other friendlies.

Wrexham spent their pre-season on a tour of the United States, playing three Premier League opponents.



They beat Leeds 3-2 in their first clash but were beaten 1-0 by Liverpool and then lost by the same scoreline to Sunderland.

However, Parkinson's men did win 1-0 against Manchester United in Finland before heading to the States.

Sports.title: Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?
Sports.content:
Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?

The 2026/27 season will begin with the Carabao Cup on Thursday and run over the weekend after a major change was made by the EFL.

Following an exciting summer of World Cup football, the return of domestic competition is getting ever closer.

2 The Carabao Cup, won by Man City last season, is getting started this week Credit: Getty

And the Carabao Cup is always one of the first competitions on the calendar - but not usually the very first...

Typically, it would be the EFL kicking things off, with Championship, League One and League Two fixtures scheduled.

However, they won't be happening for another week and instead, it's the first round of the cup that begins the campaign.

Why is the Carabao Cup first round being played over the weekend?

The Carabao Cup first round was officially moved to the weekend commencing August 7-9 in January.

It was announced that, following consultation with clubs, rather than having the cup games in midweek following the league season's opener, they would be taking place over a weekend instead.

That represented a huge change made by the EFL, considering the Carabao Cup is traditionally always played in midweek.

The switch also means that players have more rest at the start of the season, having a week's break between games, rather than playing three matches during the first week of the campaign.

The statement released at the start of 2026 read: "The EFL start dates for the 2026/27 season have been confirmed, with Round One of the Carabao Cup set to kick off the new campaign, before the Sky Bet Championship, Sky Bet League One and Sky Bet League Two begin the following weekend.

"The 2026/27 season will see Round One of the Carabao Cup take place over the weekend of 7-9 August, with the League action set to start a week later over the weekend of 14-16 August."

So, the first round fixtures take place this weekend - and in fact, the season opener between Bristol City and Walsall is being played on Thursday night having been moved earlier due to a bizarre reason.

2 The EFL made a major change to the schedule to start the season with the cup competition Credit: Getty
