Sports.title: Tottenham tipped to sign Savinho and ‘vanilla bomba’ to conclude summer transfer haul
Sports.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have been tipped to wrap up their bust summer transfer window with two further attacking additions.

This was suggested on Inside Spurs, with the panel hesitant about whether Roberto De Zerbi's 'bomba' signing will be as exciting as first billed.



4 Spurs have been active in the summer transfer market, making Sandro Tonali their club-record signing Credit: Tottenham Hotspur FC

4 Tonali arrived just days after Mateus Fernandes completed his £85million switch across the capital Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Spurs have been incredibly active in the transfer market following their brush with relegation last season.

The north London side finished two points clear of the bottom three and only secured their top-flight safety on the final day of the campaign.



As such, Spurs have strengthened at the back and in midfield, including twice breaking their club-record transfer to initially sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle, respectively.

Attention now turns to the attack, and De Zerbi hinted that a 'bomba' was imminent during the club's pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia.



The Italian clarified his comments, but supporters still believe that a 'bomba' will be dropped before long.

Who is Spurs' next 'bomba' going to be?

And Snelling expects two more attacking players to come in before the transfer window closes next month, though one of the proposed additions hardly sets the pulses racing.



On the latest episode of Inside Spurs, Majestic enquired about the mystery 'bomba' and posed the question: "Who do you think it is?"

To which Snelling replied: "Well, this is the thing. Everyone's saying: 'Will it be Savinho?'

"But to me, a 'bomba' is something that comes out of nowhere. Like a shock. Like: 'Oh my god, who is this!?'

"To me, it probably will be Cody Gakpo. I feel like that is the one.

4 Savinho has been heavily linked with a move to Tottenham over the last 12 months Credit: Getty



"I can't see Spurs going all out and getting some world-class player at this stage.

"I feel like they'll get Savinho and Gakpo, and that will be all of the business done."

'It's a vanilla 'bomba'

Snelling, though, believes Spurs should avoid signing both forwards, continuing: "Personally, I would sign one of the two.

"I'm still undecided who I think of the two because they're two completely different players.



"I'd say Gakpo is more of your like goalscorer if you want to call him that, and Savinho is more of a creative type.

"But to me, I've said it on here a few times, it would be one of them, then you sign a world-class striker.

4 Gakpo would be a "vanilla 'bomba'" according to the Inside Spurs panel Credit: Getty

"But the market's tough for strikers and maybe this is what we have to do to just get by."



Summers echoed Snelling's sentiments, adding: "Neither set my world on fire in all honesty."

"It's a vanilla 'bomba', that's what it is. Not a chocolate 'bomba'," Snelling said of Gakpo links.

"Yeah, it's a light 'bomba'," Summers agreed.

Sports.title: Ex-Manchester United assistant Rene Meulensteen joins EFL club in newly-created role
Sports.content:
League One side Stockport County have announced the appointment of Rene Meulensteen in a newly-created role.

The Hatters confirmed the Dutchman's arrival as the Director of Football Methodology on Monday.

3 Stockport County created a role specially for Rene Meulensteen Credit: Getty

"Stockport County is delighted to announce the appointment of Rene Meulensteen as the club’s new Director of Football Methodology," a statement read on the club's official website.

"The vastly experienced Dutch coach arrives at Edgeley Park having spent more than two decades working at the highest level of the game, including an immensely successful spell at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson."

"I’m delighted to be joining Stockport County as Director of Football Methodology," Meulensteen said later on Monday.

"It’s a fantastic opportunity to help build on the club’s progress and support the development of players, staff, and a clear football identity.

Meulensteen joins having last served as Graham Arnold's assistant manager for the Iraq national team between 2018 and 2024.

The appointment comes after a period of change off the pitch for Stockport.

Dave Challinor departed as manager following their League One play-off defeat to Bolton Wanderers earlier in the year.

Chief Executive Simon Wilson also left, and were replaced by Jim McNulty and Damien Allen, respectively.

McNulty admitted he is looking forward to working with Meulensteen, stating: "It is a genuine pleasure to be adding a coach of Rene Meulensteen’s calibre to our coaching team.

"Having operated at the very highest level, guided elite players, and gained invaluable experience across diverse footballing cultures in both domestic leagues and major international tournaments, he brings a tremendous breadth of wisdom and perspective to our coaching team.

3 It's been all-change off the pitch for Stockport County this summer

"This brilliant addition adds another layer of strength to our coaching collective and I am delighted Rene has decided to join our County team."

Allen, meanwhile, said: "Today marks a significant milestone in our club's history with the appointment of our first-ever Director of Football Methodology.

"His landmark appointment reflects our commitment to building an elite football department, where every player and coach across the club is aligned behind a clear football philosophy, coaching methodology, identity and way of working.

"We are delighted to welcome Rene to the club. His wealth of experience, football knowledge and proven success at the highest level will bring invaluable expertise to our coaching department.

"He will work closely with our first-team staff throughout the training week and on matchdays, while playing a pivotal role in the development of our football programme across the academy and first team.

Who is Rene Meulensteen?

The 62-year-old is best remembered for his time on the Manchester United coaching staff.

With Sir Alex Ferguson at the helm and the Dutchman part of the backroom set-up, United won the Premier League three times and the Champions League once before departing Old Trafford in 2013 after David Moyes took charge.

3 Meulensteen was briefly in charge of Fulham

Meulensteen briefly managed Anzhi Makhachkala, following up his stint in Russia with the role of Fulham boss in November 2013.

However, he was relieved of his duties in February 2014 as Felix Magath took charge at Craven Cottage.

Meulensteen returned to management in 2016 with Israeli outfit Maccabi Haifa and then on to Indian side Kerala Blasters in 2017 before taking up his position as Arnold's assistant for Iraq.

Sports.title: Liverpool need Trent Alexander-Arnold, he will unlock struggling star’s potential
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold is the perfect player to unlock Liverpool's club-record signing Alexander Isak.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor amid talk of a potentially controversial return to Anfield for the right-back.



3 Alexander-Arnold contentiously left Liverpool for Real Madrid on a free last summer Credit: Getty

Alexander-Arnold contentiously left Liverpool for Real Madrid last summer, departing his boyhood club for the La Liga giants on a free transfer.

The English right-back, who was overlooked by Thomas Tuchel for the 2026 World Cup, endured a disappointing debut campaign in Spain as he managed just 14 league starts in an injury-hit season.

The addition of Dutchman Denzel Dumfries may further limit the 27-year-old's game time under Jose Mourinho in the upcoming campaign.



In the same transfer window Alexander-Arnold signed for Madrid, Isak completed his Premier League record transfer to Anfield, though the Swedish hitman struggled in his debut campaign on Merseyside, scoring just four goals for the club so far.

Liverpool 'need' Trent

And Agbonlahor believes that the best way for Liverpool to maximise Isak's talent is to bring Alexander-Arnold back to the Reds.



Speaking with Ade Oladipo on Drive, the former Aston Villa star said: "What's crazy is when you look at Liverpool now, they need him.

"They need Trent more than they needed him before. Because now, yes, [Sadio] Mane, and [Mohamed] Salah, and [Roberto] Firmino did start to get in the box maybe. But you've got your number nine, your focal point now, no Salah anymore."



Liverpool signed Jeremie Frimpong from Bayer Leverkusen last year to replace Alexander-Arnold.

Agbonlahor, though, believes that the Dutchman's skill set doesn't match what Liverpool need, continuing: "Isak is the main guy. What does he need? Great delivery. He's not going to get that from [Jeremie] Frimpong.

3

"Frimpong's a wing-back who's quick and he can get past a couple of players.



"He can't defend. I've seen him defend one v one, can't defend. His final ball is horrendous.

"So even like Isak's probably thinking I need some better delivery from that right hand side."

'I'll take him back'

Presenter and Liverpool fan Oladipo was asked whether he'd welcome Trent back given the manner of which he left, as he said: "I'll take him back...

"I'll take him back because the options at right-back are so bad. If Conor Bradley was fit, I'd say, give Conor another go.



"I don't think Frimpong's going to work. No. I always feel like that's an exercise that hasn't worked.

"Everyone should move on from it. He's not a right winger. He's not a full-back. I mean, he didn't get in the Dutch squad for the World Cup.

3 Alexander-Arnold has played 354 games for Liverpool... so far

"And that's not the best of squads. So that's not going to work. And Conor's always injured. I'll take him back."



Agbonlahor and Oladipo's comments come after Andros Townsend suggested that Liverpool 'should not turn their nose up' at the chance to bring Alexander-Arnold back to the club.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Townsend said: "He doesn't need another season like he had last time.

"That would have been a big disappointment to him. Secretly, he would have been a little hurt that it never happened, he never really got going and had a few injury issues.

"I think Liverpool should, if they can get any deal done for him on a loan basis for a season, whatever those fees are now, up to £10million for a season, I wouldn't turn your nose up at that to get that boy back through the door.



"He is top, top drawer."

Sports.title: Aleksander Ceferin wants Club World Cup boycott as he plots Gianni Infantino downfall with Nasser Al-Khelaifi talks
Sports.content:
UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin is planning face-to-face talks with Nasser Al-Khelaifi at the Super Cup final on August 12.

Al-Khelaifi is one of Ceferin’s key allies and talkSPORT understands the UEFA President is pushing for European Football Clubs (EFC), chaired by Al-Khelaifi, to boycott the 2029 Club World Cup.

4 The walls are closing in on FIFA president Gianni Infantino with a potential Club World Cup boycott after a UEFA World Cup boycott last week Credit: Getty

However, this would require club-wide engagement with the 850+ members. Ceferin has made no secret of his own opposition to the Club World Cup, calling it a 'selfish endeavour' by Infantino back in May 2018.

The inaugural 32-team edition was won by Chelsea last summer, but plans for the 2029 event remain completely up in the air. No location or financing has yet been determined, and it is not covered by any current FIFA/EFC agreement.

Infantino has been hoping to expand the tournament to 48 teams, as well as launch a women's edition. The EFC was broadly supportive of the 2025 plans despite tensions in the lead-up to the tournament, and Al-Khelaifi played a pivotal role in determining the funding model.

Yet a major sticking point is promised solidarity payments from the 2025 edition have not yet been settled with many clubs demanding payment from FIFA.

The proposed 2029 Club World Cup lacks key foundational elements such as a location, funding structure, format or sponsors, and the tournament would not gain EFC support unless that changes.

Ceferin, meanwhile, wants the EFC to go public saying they will no longer work with FIFA on the Club World Cup while Infantino remains in charge.

UEFA are mobilising on a concerted effort for Infantino to resign. Ceferin has led calls for a blanket withdraw of letters in support of Infantino, and on Monday the Welsh FA confirmed they had revoked their endorsement pointing towards "recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement."

The English FA are yet to release a statement, but talkSPORT understands they will also remove their support of Infantino.

Who wants to be president?

Ceferin himself has no plans to stand for FIFA president, but would support Al-Khelaifi doing so. The two will meet during the showpiece Super Cup clash between PSG and Aston Villa.

4 Ceferin is furious with Infantino but has no plans to stand against him

In fact, several UEFA Member Associations would back the Qatari executive to go head-to-head against Infantino even though sources close to the PSG president say he has 'no ambition' to do so, according to a a spokesperson.

There is a growing sense within UEFA that it might be better to back a candidate from outside the confederation in order to gain more votes. UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told Hawksbee & Jacobs Infantino needs a rival if he doesn't quit.

"I think there has to be a candidate against Infantino now, and the important thing is that candidate can unite the opposition to him across the world," said the former Wales international.

"Clearly we have made our voice heard, as have the Asian federation (AFC) and Concacaf, but we need to have a candidate that can really unite the world to ensure he or she is capable of beating Infantino."

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is giving serious thought to standing, and his confederation carries a further 35 votes. Alignment between UEFA and Concacaf could take a candidate to a maximum 90 votes, needing just 16 more for a majority.

However, Switzerland released a statement saying they want a 'personal exchange' with Infantino before determining next steps, while Czech Republic FA President David Trunda initially backed Infantino's controversial privatisation plans, even though UEFA's subsequent statement against FIFA Forward Enterprise made it clear all 55 members were opposed.

4 Al-Khelaifi is well thought of by Ceferin and other figures in European football but does not want Infantino's job Credit: Getty

Many insiders believe both Infantino and Montagliani are currently doing the maths to inform their position, but Ceferin is now hoping to either persuade Al-Khelaifi to stand or to get behind Montagliani.

UEFA insiders want a singular candidate to come forward believing it will encourage other federations to back them publicly.

talkSPORT can also reveal there are calls from some senior leaders for the remit and title of the FIFA president to be changed entirely into more of a ‘chair’ role.

This would see an elected official supported by a small inner circle of vice-chairs, representative of various bodies, that collectively report into the FIFA Council thus creating more checks and balances.

It would essentially found an executive leadership team rather than a sole leader. That could be a way of convincing Al-Khelaifi, as well as some high-profile confederation heads, to be back this proposal and even be involved

Infantino is also in many ways already campaigning having personally reached out to several federations. Saudi Arabia and Qatar were two of the first to back him, showing Asia, a key battleground, is not as united in its position as UEFA.

4 The World Cup proved to be something of a circus at points Credit: Getty

Bangladesh, Morocco, Kuwait, UAE, Bhutan and Sri Lanka are other federations to issue statements of support. It is clear Infantino hasn't lost much, if any, support in Africa.

The challenge for Infantino is even with these federations on side, UEFA now intend to bring FIFA into logistical and commercial gridlock, including a proposed Club World Cup boycott.

And Infantino must also deal with a divided leadership team, with several figures close to him wanting him to resign rather than faces months of instability.

Ceferin will hope by the time the Super Cup arrives, Infantino has already been persuaded to quit.

But those close to the Infantino are adamant it is not in his nature to stand down, and that his ability to pull off a 2026 World Cup that, as the FIFA President put it, 'destroyed all records' and needed 'new words to define the success' will keep a base of support – as will his ability to provide increased funding to member federations.

talkSPORT has contacted FIFA for comment.

Sports.title: UFC fighter, 34, found dead after 'apparent heart attack' in his sleep
Sports.content:
UFC fighter Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an 'apparent heart attack' in his sleep.

It comes just six weeks after the Brazilian's last fight in Las Vegas on June 20. He suffered a split decision loss to Mitch Raposo at UFC Vegas 119.

A UFC statement read: 'This morning, Monday, August 3rd, our beloved flyweight fighter, Allan Nascimento, was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

'Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene.

'Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan's family, friends, teammates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.'

The UFC's statement was accompanied by a single black-and-white photo of him smiling, while holding up his fist in a UFC boxing glove.

UFC star Allan Nascimento has died at the age of 34 after suffering an 'apparent heart attack'

It comes just six weeks after the Brazilian (left) lost last fight in Las Vegas on June 20

Nascimento finished his career with a 22-7 professional record, winning four of six UFC fights

Born in Sao Paulo, Nascimento built an impressive reputation by winning 17 of his first 22 fights.

A flyweight, the 'Puro Osso' - a Portuguese idiom meaning 'skin and bones' - competed in multiple promotions during his career, including RIZIN, Legacy FC and Dana White's Contender Series.

Nascimento then joined the UFC in 2021 and won four of his six fights. He finished his career with a 22-7 professional record.

He managed to secure the Performance of the Night bonuses for impressing fans in submission victories over Carlos Hernandez and Cody Durden.

Former UFC lightweight champion Charles Oliveira, who trained with Nascimento in Sao Paulo, posted an emotional tribute on social media.

He wrote in Portuguese: 'Today I lost a brother that the fight game gave me. Thank you for always being by my side, for sharing the mats and the corner.

'I have nothing but gratitude for having you with me - in training, in the corner, and just hanging out. I love you, man; you're a legend. My brother, I can’t even believe it; you will be deeply missed.'

Sports.title: What Morgan Gibbs-White's agent change means for Nottingham Forest future: Oliver Glasner's role, the boost for Bayern Munich, interest from Chelsea and where boyhood club Man United stand
Sports.content:
The transfer news was announced across social media by a user with more than 100 million followers and designed for maximum exposure.

The player in question is Morgan Gibbs-White although – until now at least – he has not changed clubs this summer. Rather, the Nottingham Forest No10 has decided to switch representatives, from the powerful CAA Stellar to ROOF, an emerging force in the world of football agents, and the news came through football transfer influencer Fabrizio Romano.

ROOF's headquarters are in Germany and as well as Gibbs-White, they represent Kai Havertz, Virgil van Dijk, Ademola Lookman and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler.

When players move to a new agency, the usual conclusion is that they are looking for a way out. While that is not necessarily the case with Gibbs-White, the move certainly raised eyebrows across the game, not least among the Forest hierarchy.

Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at where Forest and Gibbs-White stand and what might happen next.

When players move to a new agency, the usual conclusion is they are looking for a way out. While that is not necessarily the case with Gibbs-White, it raised eyebrows across the game

Gibbs-White (furthest left) is coming off the best season of his career, scoring 15 Premier League goals and 18 in all competitions

What is Forest’s stance?

Unless the offer is too attractive to turn down, Forest’s position is that they have no intention of selling Gibbs-White this summer.

With Elliot Anderson sold to Manchester City for £116million, there is little pressure on Forest to bring in cash from sales and owner Evangelos Marinakis does not want to let another star player go in the same window.

Having hired Oliver Glasner as coach, Marinakis’ plan is to improve, rather than simply consolidate. The idea is to build the new-look Forest around Gibbs-White, who missed out on a place in England’s World Cup squad despite 18 goals and seven assists in all competitions last season.

When Gibbs-White’s move to Tottenham last summer did not go through, he signed a new three-year deal at Forest, making him the highest-paid player in the club’s history. Forest’s plan then was to put Gibbs-White at the heart of everything and, after his brilliant 2025-26, they are not about to change tack.

They also believe Glasner’s arrival can take Gibbs-White’s game to another level – just as he did with Adam Wharton, Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze at Crystal Palace. But to achieve this, Glasner needs Gibbs-White to be fully committed, and not with one eye on a move.

Tottenham thought they had triggered Gibbs-White's release clause last summer. Forest thought otherwise and he signed a new contract

New Forest boss Oliver Glasner (right) was brilliant at turning players into stars at Crystal Palace, such as Michael Olise (left)

What is Gibbs-White’s mindset?

This summer and last, Gibbs-White has watched team-mates join Champions League clubs while he has stayed put. Last July, Anthony Elanga moved to Newcastle and this year it was Anderson’s turn to depart. Anderson, incidentally, is represented by Stellar.

This time a year ago, Tottenham believed they had activated a £60million release clause in Gibbs-White’s contract – but Forest thought otherwise and they won the day. Gibbs-White is very well compensated and is settled in Nottingham, where the Forest supporters adore him.

He would not be human, though, if the transfers of Anderson and Elanga had not affected his thinking. If they were good enough to play in the Champions League, Gibbs-White might have wondered, then why wasn’t he? While not necessarily unhappy at Forest, Gibbs-White is ambitious.

He was also bitterly disappointed to be left out by England boss Thomas Tuchel for this summer’s tournament despite turning in the best season of his career, scoring 15 Premier League goals to steer Forest away from relegation.

Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Chelsea showed a growing interest in Gibbs-White earlier this summer but the 26-year-old aspires to play as high as he can and that means the Champions League. He was a boyhood Manchester United fan who idolised Wayne Rooney, while at least once Manchester City have moved for him without taking the final step.

Indeed, Gibbs-White thought he was on his way to City in summer 2025, only for City to sign Rayan Cherki instead for half the cost of the England man's release clause.

As for United, it is thought their priorities currently lie elsewhere, with Bruno Fernandes producing a sensational campaign last term. Daily Mail Sport reported last February that Gibbs-White was seen as a potential replacement for Fernandes were he to leave United this summer but at this stage there appears little prospect of the Portuguese playmaker changing clubs.

This summer and last, Gibbs-White has watched team-mates such as Elliot Anderson (right) join Champions League clubs while he has stayed put

He was a boyhood Manchester United fan who idolised Wayne Rooney, while at least once Manchester City have moved for him without taking the final step

How will this play out?

It is understood that Glasner’s arrival has already had a positive impact on Gibbs-White. At the end of last season, with Forest finishing 16th and losing in the semi-finals of the Europa League, Gibbs-White was assessing his options.

Would he ever fulfil his Champions League dream by staying at Forest? In three of their four seasons since promotion, Forest have been fighting at the wrong end of the table. Last season they finished 16 points adrift of Liverpool, who claimed the final Champions League spot. That is a heck of a gap to bridge.

Gibbs-White is said to have been energised by Glasner’s arrival and has been particularly impressed with the Austrian during Forest’s recent training camp in Portugal. Gibbs-White will also be keeping a close eye on new signings. Will these, plus the arrival of a proven winner in the dugout, be enough to stop his head being turned?

Intriguingly, Daily Mail Sport understands that if Michael Olise leaves Bayern Munich this summer, Gibbs-White would be among the candidates to replace him. Olise is wanted by Real Madrid.

It is worth noting that ROOF have strong links with Bayern, who have recruited extremely well from the Premier League recently by signing Olise in 2024, and Harry Kane a year earlier. Historically, English clubs are more amenable to selling their top players overseas than to domestic rivals, which could also work in Bayern’s favour.

ROOF have strong links with Bayern Munich, who have recruited extremely well from the Premier League recently by signing Olise in 2024, and Harry Kane a year earlier

Gibbs-White is now at the centre of the Forest project and would expect to be treated as such

Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal are also seeking an attacking midfielder to play alongside former Wolves captain Ruben Neves, ex-West Ham winger Crysencio Summerville and 2022 Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema, yet it would be a huge step for Gibbs-White to move there in the prime of his career, and with his England dream still alive.

If Gibbs-White moves this summer, it may well be overseas. If he stays one more year, there would be other options – perhaps United, if this is to be Fernandes’ final season.

When Forest signed Gibbs-White for £25m plus add-ons after promotion in 2022, then-boss Steve Cooper assured him he would be properly backed even in periods of poor form, which had never happened at boyhood club Wolves.

He is now at the centre of the Forest project and whenever he moves, Gibbs-White will expect similar treatment. The next few weeks promise to be very interesting.

Sports.title: Henry Pollock the million-pound player? Why Eddie Hearn's sums don't add up, the reality of the French threat and how this will all likely end
Sports.content:
When Henry Pollock became the first rugby player to sign with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency in March, it was a positive shift for the sport.

The English club game has struggled financially and its players have, with a few exceptions, struggled to cut through into mainstream society. Hearn’s arrival into the game was viewed as a means of changing that, raising the profiles of Pollock and Scotland No 10 Finn Russell who also joined the stable and by extension, that of rugby too. It all seemed rather positive.

Almost immediately, however, Hearn questioned how much Pollock was earning through his contracts with club Northampton Saints and England. He vowed to soon increase that.

On Monday, Hearn went one step further. He told The Daily Telegraph that Pollock, still just 21 and with a grand total of one start for England under his belt, was deserving of a Northampton salary of £1million a year.

This was on the basis that he is a player who brings a unique combination of undoubted on-field talent as well as significant commercial benefits to the sport he plays. ‘He's certainly a seven-figure player,’ Hearn said. ‘The way rugby's going and what Pollock is doing, his value over the next couple of years will skyrocket and I think the value of rugby will.’

Hearn is right about one thing. Pollock has been a breath of fresh air to English rugby. He is supremely talented and although not universally popular, he is exactly the sort of player the sport needs to grow. Where Hearn is misguided, however, is on the numbers.

When Henry Pollock became the first rugby player to sign with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency in March, it was a positive shift for the sport

Pollock has been a breath of fresh air to English rugby. He is supremely talented and although not universally popular, he is exactly the sort of player the sport needs to grow

Pollock’s current Northampton contract – which, and the timing is crucial to Hearn's words, expires next summer – is worth £150,000 and his status as an Enhanced Elite Playing Squad (EEPS) member with England also earns him roughly the same again from the RFU.

But in English rugby’s current financial climate, it is simply inconceivable for Northampton – or indeed any of the other nine PREM Rugby teams – to pay Pollock such a sum. Even with the investment coming into the league, the money just does not exist in this country right now.

It would great if it did as it would reflect significant growth across the English game. But, unfortunately, it does not. It is pie in the sky. The only possible side who could go to such lengths is Newcastle Red Bulls following their takeover by the energy drink giants, though that is unlikely.

Even the richest French clubs, in their thriving system full of money, would likely baulk at such a figure - and, of course, would require Pollock to give up his England career by playing overseas.

Antoine Dupont, still the biggest star in the world game, earns £1.2million a year at Toulouse, but Pollock is not on the France scrum-half's level, in talent or earnings power. England heavyweights Owen Farrell and Maro Itoje would have earned close to £1million at Saracens - but that was before the EEPS contracts came in, where the RFU covers some of the player's salary to lower the burden on clubs.

But really, it is irrelevant. Pollock does not want to leave Northampton. It is also pointless Hearn comparing Pollock’s income with that of his boxing clients. It is like comparing chalk with cheese. Rugby, unfortunately, remains far behind boxing and miles off football in terms of the wealth within the sport.

There is no doubt that Pollock’s rapid ascent from an academy player to a regular England international and British & Irish Lion is unusual for one so young. As such, he is certainly deserving of an increase from £150,000.

But Hearn’s demands are likely to cause a problem for Northampton. All PREM teams are limited to a playing squad spend of £6.4m, with the salary of one ‘marquee’ player allowed outside that figure. Northampton are a club who do not spend up to the maximum in a bid to ensure financial stability, making their league titles in 2024 and 2026 all the more impressive.

There is no doubt that Pollock’s rapid ascent to a regular England international and British & Irish Lion is unusual for one so young. He is certainly deserving of an increase

Northampton do not spend close to the PREM Rugby salary cap, which makes their recent titles in 2024 and 2026 all the more impressive

It is unlikely that the Saints hierarchy of director of rugby Phil Dowson and chief executive Julia Chapman will blow their team’s modus operandi into smithereens at Hearn’s demands, even if they will clearly want to keep hold of Pollock. They have other high-class England stars to keep happy too, namely Fin Smith, Tommy Freeman and Alex Mitchell.

Another complication is that when Pollock and Russell announced their Matchroom deals, it was confirmed that their then-representative Matt Hart of Stellar Group, would remain in charge of their playing contracts.

That is still the case. But Hearn’s comments do raise an interesting question as to who will be leading the negotiating with Northampton. Hearn and Hart are working collaboratively with Pollock, but the former’s comments have certainly rocked the boat.

The likely result of all this is a compromise. Pollock will get an increase, though it is almost certain to fall well short of Hearn’s demands. The player, however, is likely to in time get close to being the million-pound man through additional commercial contracts alongside his Northampton and England deals. And that can only be a good thing for him and rugby as a whole.

Sports.title: Brawling football fans rip out seats as riot police are called in and match is suspended - with nearly 2,000 supporters fleeing onto the pitch for safety
Sports.content:
Brawling football fans rip out seats as riot police are called in and match is suspended - with nearly 2,000 supporters fleeing onto the pitch for safety

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Football fans in Colombia were involved in nasty clashes on Sunday as riot police were forced to intervene.

During Atletico Nacional's 3-0 victory over Jaguares de Cordoba in the Colombian top flight, play was suspended during the first half when supporters became embroiled in a violent brawl.

Footage from the match showed fans ripping out seats and throwing them at each other before riot police rushed into action.

This led to the referee halting the game at the Estadio Jaraguay in Monteria, a city in northern Colombia, with both sets of players taken into the dressing room during the suspension.

At the time, Atletico had raced into a three-goal lead, with former Rangers striker Alfredo Morelos among the scorers.

During the chaotic scenes, an estimated 2,000 supporters fled onto the pitch to escape the trouble, with footage on social media showing the extent of what had gone on.

🚨🇨🇴 Clashes broke out in the stands during the Jaguares vs. Atlético Nacional match in Monteria. Fans were seen throwing stadium chairs as riot police intervened, causing a temporary stoppage in the game. 😳 pic.twitter.com/vj6ZLef5lw — Ultras Clips (@ultras_clips) August 3, 2026

Jaguares 0-3 Atlético Nacional

Fecha 2

⚽️ 7' Marlon Moreno

⚽️ 19' Andrés Sarmiento

⚽️ 32' Alfredo Morelos

🏟 Algunos aficionados invadieron el gramado del Estadio Jaraguay de Monteria.

🚨 42' Partido suspendido y cuerpos técnicos con jugadores permanancen en los camerinos. pic.twitter.com/Ir1y6D4xzO — 🎙Juan Pablo Rúa Jiménez🎙 (@JuanPabloRuaJim) August 2, 2026

Violent scenes broke out at a Colombian football match as fans threw seats at each other

Thousands of fans fled onto the pitch in an attempt to escape the trouble inside the stadium

It was widely reported that the trouble involved Atletico fans, who were the away team, fighting among themselves.

Monteria Metropolitan Police later revealed that one officer suffered a serious leg injury amid the shocking scenes.

20 people were also treated for minor injuries, while 300 supporters were thrown out of the ground following the trouble.

After the suspension in play, which lasted just over 30 minutes, the referee did restart the game.

Yet that wasn't the end of the drama as Atletico were reduced to 10 men when Andres Felipe Roman was sent off, although they held on for a 3-0 victory.

Atletico are one of the biggest teams in Colombia, winning the Copa Libertadores on two occasions and the Colombian title 18 times.

Some of their notable former players include Rene Higuita, Andres Escobar, Davinson Sanchez and David Ospina.

Sports.title: Plot to 'paralyse' Gianni Infantino: FIFA president's opponents 'form alliance to stage their own international tournaments if he refuses to step down' after World Cup sell-off disgrace
Sports.content:
The leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have reportedly formed an alliance aimed at toppling Gianni Infantino.

The FIFA president is under huge pressure after he was forced to abandon a hugely controversial proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, following a major revolt from the footballing world.

UEFA subsequently declared a loss of confidence in the Italian-Swiss administrator, while the English and Welsh FA are among several countries to withdraw their support for his re-election in next March's elections.

This has left Infantino fighting for his job, and he reportedly held crunch talks with the White House on Monday in a bid to help him survive.

And now, according to The Times, the leaders of the three confederations are preparing to 'paralyse FIFA' if he refuses to resign.

The report adds that they have several plans in place if the FIFA President insists on remaining in power and seeking re-election at next March's election.

Gianni Infantino's opponents have formed an alliance in an attempt to force him to resign

The alliance includes the leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC (pictured - Infantino with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024)

This includes being prepared to stage their own rival international competitions, while they are also willing to impose a 'government boycott'.

This would effectively mean they would refuse to either ratify FIFA decisions or be involved in council and committee meetings.

A source told The Times: 'Everyone is very determined he needs to go, and if not we will take all the necessary steps [to remove him from power].

'That includes future international competitions - would the big South American countries prefer to play France or Spain, or Lebanon or Djibouti? Everyone is very determined, there are no backward steps now.'

It is also believed that with several countries withdrawing their support for Infantino, he has only secured the backing of around 15 nations so far.

Back in the summer, it was understood that the 56-year-old had the support of nearly all of the 211 FIFA members for his re-election in March. He needs 106 votes to win.

No candidates have yet come forward to challenge him though, and they only have until November 18 to do so.

If a significant number of nations called for Infantino to quit, it may help generate support for an emergency FIFA council meeting.

The English and Welsh FA are among the nations to withdraw their support for Infantino

Daily Mail Sport also reported earlier on Monday how several European nations, including England and Wales, had formally withdrawn their backing for the beleaguered football chief.

At the weekend, the FA had called for 'a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently'.

A statement from the Welsh FA on Monday then read: 'The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr. Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027–2031 term.

'The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr. Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.'

Serbia, Sweden and Finland also publicly withdrew their support, although Morocco, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait and Sri Lanka were among those to back Infantino.

The latest update in this saga comes after UEFA sent Infantino a legal letter on Friday, where it threatened legal action over the abandoned plot, before adding that documents relating to the plan, known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), must be preserved.

The letter to Infantino read: 'Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below.

'You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.'

UEFA went on to warn FIFA that 'any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment or loss of relevant materials' after their letter 'may constitute spoliation of evidence'.

They then refused to rule out further action if any of the aforementioned actions took place, but the letter itself is not legal action.

The letter also insisted that FIFA must ensure that certain individuals, including Infantino, Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and Kevin Lamour, FIFA's chief operating officer, 'specifically preserve all such materials in their possession'.

UEFA later confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that a document preservation letter was sent.

Sports.title: Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea confirmed: England midfielder, 36, joins Blues after ripping up Brentford contract
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed their signing of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, after Brentford allowed the 36-year-old to terminate his contract a year earlier than expected.

It comes two days after they secured the signature of Danny Welbeck, 35, from Brighton.

Between them, Henderson and Welbeck will add 863 Premier League games’ worth of experience to a changing room now overseen by new manager Xabi Alonso, 44.

Henderson said: 'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down.

‘I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

‘For me, it's about giving everything every single day, both on and off the field, to help the players around me and the team as much as possible. I'm very excited to get going.’

Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea has been confirmed after he ripped up his Brentford deal

The midfielder was all smiles as he spent the day at Chelsea's Cobham training ground

Henderson, 36, said he was ready to 'give everything every single day, on and off the field'

Alonso identified during his talks to take over Chelsea that their squad was in need of greater balance among the players. The Blues had broken Premier League records for fielding the youngest sides over the previous two seasons, but they had been criticised by fans on occasion for appearing to lack maturity on and off the pitch.

Chelsea previously targeted Granit Xhaka, the 33-year-old Sunderland captain who had worked with Alonso at Bayer Leverkusen, but were unable to get him out of the Stadium of Light. They likewise showed interest in John Stones, who has now joined Inter Milan at 32.

Yet they have now secured Henderson for free, while the fee for Welbeck is being described as ‘undisclosed’, though his cost is by no means substantial, if indeed there even is one.

Welbeck has already travelled to Hong Kong to join his new team-mates. Daily Mail Sport reported last week how Brentford were ready to sanction Henderson’s exit rather than seek a fee from Chelsea. He is still recovering from the broken arm he suffered with England at the World Cup.

These signings are concrete confirmation that Chelsea have adjusted their transfer strategy by now aiming to add experienced leaders to their squad. Previously, there had been a focus on finding younger players of potential.

Maxence Lacroix, 26 and from Crystal Palace, has already been confirmed by Chelsea for £52million. Morgan Rogers has also arrived for £117m from Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Celtic 1-0 Dundee: Benjamin Nygren gets the job done as home side huff and puff on flag night
Sports.content:
Celtic 1-0 Dundee: Benjamin Nygren gets the job done as home side huff and puff on flag night

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

For the 14th time in 15 years, Celtic hoisted the league flag to rapturous applause in Glasgow’s East End.

It was the failure of the hierarchy to sufficiently raise the standard of player since that cherished prize was claimed in May which made the peace which followed a distinctly uneasy one.

Some 79 days after seeing his side retain their crown in the most dramatic fashion imaginable against Hearts, Martin O’Neill will have been pleased that the defence started with a slender victory which was just about merited on the balance of play.

But the bigger picture for all and sundry was impossible to escape. Some 14 players who were around the club last season have since left — including the talismanic Daizen Maeda, without whom the campaign would assuredly have had a different ending.

While the two players who have come in — Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh — should be excellent additions, the depth of the squad at this juncture is alarming.

Where’s the goalkeeper to push or displace Viljami Sinisalo? What’s the plan to provide much-needed cover for Kieran Tierney at left back? And where on earth are the raft of midfielders and wingers that O’Neill evidently needs if this campaign isn’t to turn into another almighty struggle?

Benjamin Nygren rises to head home the only goal of the game against Dundee at Celtic Park

Hyun-jun Yang tries a shot on goal during a match in which Celtic laboured to create chances

Skipper Callum McGregor holds the Premiership trophy ahead of kick-off at Celtic Park

With Austrian champions LASK on the horizon in the Champions League play-off, the board have just about enough time to turn this situation around, but their procrastination is seeing them play an extremely dangerous game.

For the most part, Celtic were lethargic and predictable. Lacking in guile until they made the breakthrough, they laboured to create many clear-cut opportunities. This is a team that’s crying out for an infusion of forward-thinking players.

After a forgettable opening half, they improved to a degree and got there through Benjamin Nygren’s flashing header just after the turnaround. The Swede managed 21 goals last term and clearly cannot be relied on to the same extent.

Notwithstanding the fact that these occasions are often sticky affairs that don’t yield many goals, the need for new recruits to arrive in short order was absolutely glaring. There’s an awful lot of work to be done if the flag-raising ceremony is to take place again this time next year.

Dundee didn’t leave with anything tangible to show for their efforts, but the fact they competed to the last will have pleased their manager, Steven Pressley.

Seeking to record a first win at this ground since 2001, the frustration for the Dark Blues followers was that they didn’t really do enough in the final third to capitalise on Celtic’s obvious vulnerability.

Paradoxically, the lack of new signings to this point did give O’Neill one less thing to think about.

Faced with such limited options on the flanks, Duran dropped out to the right while record signing Hogh played through the middle. For now, last season’s 4-3-3 remains.

With Liam Scales suspended, Auston Trusty began beside Cameron Carter-Vickers. This was the latter’s first appearance since featuring against Sturm Graz on October 23 when Brendan Rodgers was the manager.

Alistair Johnston and Arne Engels started despite ongoing interest from Everton and West Ham, respectively.

Since impressively finishing eighth last term, Dundee had seen pivotal figures including Billy Koumetio, Luke Graham, Tony Yogane and Cam Congreve go out the door.

Fresh from signing a new contract, Pressley started four of the replacements — Owen Goodman, Idris Odutayo, Owen Bevan and Ryan Finnigan. They all acquitted themselves well.

The Dark Blues enjoyed the advantage of having four League Cup group stage games under their belt. Their sharpness was evident as they gave little up in the opening exchanges.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Celtic took a while to warm to the task. Hyun-jun Yang saw an early effort blocked by Joe Westley with Hogh then sending Nygren’s square ball the wrong side of the post.

At times, Hogh looked a little too anxious to make a telling impact. Again, played in by Nygren after fine play from Tierney, Goodman in the visiting goal was left untroubled by his shot.

The Dane did better when Nygren fed him for a third time after Yang’s interception. Bevan’s timely tackle sent the ball for a corner.

Yang looked the most likely home player to find the breakthrough. An ambitious dribble to take him away from three men ended with Ryan Astley stopping to block.

An untimely slip by Callum McGregor gave Joe Bevan sight of goal. Tierney was on hand to get his body in the way of the shot.

With Dundee enjoying a spell of pressure in and around Celtic’s box, Owen Bevan’s dipping header was watched all the way by Sinisalo.

Although O’Neill’s players saw plenty of the ball, they didn’t seem to be on the same page. That said, Tierney’s excellent cross for Engels ought to have brought the opener. The Belgian’s header drifted beyond the far post.

Credit to referee Matthew MacDermid for allowing Celtic a potential advantage when Hogh was felled on the half-way line. It allowed Engels to feed the overlapping Tierney. The full-back’s meaty strike was smartly punched away by Goodman.

O’Neill would have demanded more at the break. Much more. And, in fairness, Celtic lifted the tempo and began asking more questions.

Arriving on 52 minutes, the opener stemmed from McGregor taking the ball from Sinisalo and recognising Engels was in a position to do some damage.

Yang emerged to keep the move flowing then turned back to feed Tierney. His cross had pace and curl. Nygren clinically nodded home from six yards. The relief in the arena was palpable.

It was better from the champions from that point on. More passes found their intended targets, more one-on-ones were won, space was better exploited. That said, it required an outstanding recovery run from Trusty to prevent Joe Bevan from going clear on goal on the counter.

With Dundee left with little option but to gamble, gaps appeared. Both Yang and Tierney smashed low shots on target, but they were never beating Goodman. McGregor also got under a strike after being played in by Engels’ short corner.

It said much about O’Neill’s lack of options that it took him until the 78th minute to make a change — 35-year-old James Forrest for Yang — and even that was injury-enforced.

It just wasn’t Hogh’s night. He sent another chance just wide following Colby Donovan’s low cross. McGregor then hit the upright before Forrest curled the rebound wide.

Seb Tounekti’s rising shot ensured a nervy finish. Celtic fans might see a few more of those in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes confirms arrival in La Manga as Newcastle REJECT Arsenal bid, Chelsea agree £26m deal to sell Trevoh Chalobah to Como... and Fulham complete £44.5m swoop for Real Madrid duo: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Former Man United coach lands new job at Stockport

Former Manchester United coach Rene Meulensteen has been appointed as Stockport County’s new director of football methodology.

The role will see Meulensteen oversee Stockport's football philosophy and coaching methodology working day-to-day with both the first team and academy.

The 62-year-old Dutch coach arrives at Edgeley Park from a World Cup campaign where he was assistant coach to the Iraq national team.

Fulham snap up Real Madrid stars

Fulham confirmed the twin signings of £36m striker Gonzalo Garcia and £8.5m midfielder Cesar Palacios late on Monday night.

Fulham have confirmed the £36m signing of striker Gonzalo Garcia from Real Madrid

The pair have signed five-year deals with the option to extend by a further 12 months.

'I'm very grateful, very happy to be here', Garcia told the club website.

'I have to thank the board and Arbeloa for the trust they've put in me, and I'm very, very excited to start.'

Palacios said: 'I am very emotional to be here. I believe it is the perfect step in my career.

'The Club is showing a lot of trust in me, and I'm going to show it on the pitch.'

West Ham in market for Spurs outcast

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham, as first reported in Window Watch last week.

Solomon has impressed Roberto de Zerbi during a pre season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

De Zerbi knows the Israel international well because they worked together at Shakhtar Donetsk but the winger is set to leave after failing to hold down a place in three years at Spurs.

At 27, he is only interested in a permanent move, having spent last season on loan at Villarreal and Fiorentina and the previous season on loan at Leeds, where he sparkled as they won promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Fiorentina retain an interest despite not taking up the option on a permanent deal after his loan.

West Ham are among the clubs interested in signing Manor Solomon from Tottenham

Others are also monitoring the situation, and Spurs have to sell players to clear space in De Zerbi's squad and generate more income.

West Ham are in the market for a winger after selling Crysencio Summerville, but captain Jarrod Bowen has committed his future to the Hammers despite relegation.

MATT BARLOW

Preston boss hits out with Whiteman set for exit to Wrexham

Preston North End have accepted a £3million bid from Wrexham for their wantaway captain Ben Whiteman.

Manager Paul Heckingbottom voiced his displeasure at the weekend, saying Whiteman had crossed a line after telling them he had played his last game for the club in an effort to force through the move.

'Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross and unfortunately he has,' Heckingbottom told BBC Radio Lancashire. 'There's a valuation on him, I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it otherwise he's put himself in a sticky situation. He's made his bed. I'm not bothered as long as I get another player.'

The 30-year-old midfielder is now free to have a medical and complete the transfer, with personal terms not expected to be a problem.

The deal is expected to go through in the next 48 hours and Preston are looking to reinvest the money in another three or four new signings this summer.

Paul Heckingbottom says Ben Whiteman has 'crossed a line' in making his move

Hammers plot £18m bid to land Parrott

West Ham are preparing to outbid European rivals to sign former Tottenham striker Troy Parrott.

The Hammers want to bolster their attack quickly with the new Championship season looming and after being rebuffed for Sunderland's Wilson Isidor, are targeting AZ Alkmaar forward Parrott.

The Republic of Ireland international has interest from Ajax, Como, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis but Alkmaar are reluctant to sell to a Dutch rival.

The Hammers hope an offer of around £18million will be enough to fend off the competition.

Parrott struggled while at Spurs but after an initial loan to Excelsior Rotterdam he began to find his feet and has been prolific with Alkmaar since.

Read more on this story HERE

Troy Parrott celebrates winning the Johan Cruyff Shield with Alkmaar on Sunday

Henderson's relish as he joins Chelsea

Chelsea have announced the signing of 36-year-old Jordan Henderson, after he was allowed to leave Brentford with a year left on his deal.

'Given the size of the club, the manager, who I have great admiration for, and the quality of the players, this was a huge opportunity I couldn't turn down,' Henderson said.

'I was also so impressed with how much the ownership want Chelsea to be successful and move in the right direction.

For more on this story click HERE

Jordan Henderson signs on the dotted line as he joins Xabi Alonso's Chelsea revolution

Sunderland block the door to Isidor

West Ham have asked to take Sunderland winger Simon Adingra on loan, but the Wearsiders have no plans to sell forward Wilson Isidor.

West Ham have asked about both players but after initial conversations Sunderland have made it clear that they want to keep Haiti international Isidor.

Discussions are ongoing between the clubs over a straight loan for 24-year-old Ivory Coast international Adingra.

Despite interest from a host of clubs, however, Sunderland will not entertain offers for Isidor. The 25-year-old remains an integral part of their squad ahead of their season in European competition and the club believe he can build on an excellent World Cup with Haiti.

West Ham are continuing to discuss AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott while Lazio are interested in the Hammers' German international forward Niclas Fullkrug.

Wilson Isidor is back after the World Cup and Sunderland say he is not for sale despite interest

Como agree £26m Chalobah deal... as Napoli eye Badiashile

Chelsea and Como have agreed a £26million fee for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The deal will include a further £5.2m in add-ons for the 27-year-old England centre-back who is expected to travel to Italy on Wednesday evening.

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile continues to attract interest from Napoli. The Blues are looking to recoup funds for the French centre-back as well as for Axel Disasi who has been the subject of talks with Crystal Palace and West Ham - both are discussing offers.

Disasi had a spell on loan at West Ham last season but ideally wants a top flight offer.

Chelsea hope to make progress with Rayo Vallecano over the purchase of left wing-back Pep Chavarria.

Trevoh Chalobah is on his way to Como, managed by former Blues star Cesc Fabregas

Newcastle reject Arsenal bid for Bruno as he joins Magpies in La Manga

Arsenal's opening bid for Bruno Guimaraes has been rejected by Newcastle. As reported earlier, the clubs are now in direct talks over a deal for Brazilian.

Guimaraes has landed in Spain and is travelling to report back for Newcastle's pre-season camp in La Manga today.

Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle is at La Manga with the squad and wants to meet the captain.

Bruno Guimaraes is subject of interest from Arsenal but they have not yet made a formal offer

Guimaraes confirmed his arrival in Spain on Instagram on Monday evening

Bernardo gets shirty at Real

Bernardo Silva has arrived at Real Madrid as he joins up with Jose Mourinho's side. The 31-year-old left Manchester City at the end of last season.

The Portugal star, who has returned from the World Cup, was seen signing shirts for fans after medical tests.

🚨 Bernardo Silva continue de signer quelques maillots avant de quitter Sanitas.



🎥 @ainoafrndz pic.twitter.com/7wFAeRQm2F — Le Journal du Real (@lejournaldureal) August 3, 2026

Man United would loan out Chido Obi for game time

Manchester United are willing to send striker Chido Obi Martin out on loan this summer.

The 18-year-old Denmark U21 international had interest from Cologne earlier in the window, but they have moved to sign Jaiden Heskey from Manchester City and are lining up Tottenham winger Mikey Moore.

Chido Obi joined United from Arsenal's academy in 2024 and has made seven first-team appearances though failed to score.

United want to ensure his next club is one where he can develop properly with competitive game time.

Join the queue for Everton's Tim

Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam is attracting increasing interest from rival Premier League clubs and from abroad.

Coventry City, Hull City and Ipswich Town have all made enquiries while two Italian clubs have also asked about the 23-year-old.

Lazio tried to sign the former England U20 international in January.

Everton are continuing to discuss a deal for Arsenal's Christian Norgaard which, if completed, could pave the way for Iroegbunam to depart once a suitable offer comes in.

Everton paid around £9million to Aston Villa for Iroegbunam in 2024.

Tim Iroegbunam joined from Aston Villa two years ago

Coventry keen on Mudryk

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.

Sports.title: UFC fighter Allan Nascimento, 34, found dead at home after suffering ‘heart attack’
Sports.content:
UFC fighter Allan Nascimento, 34, found dead at home after suffering ‘heart attack’

The Brazilian 'beloved fighter and exemplary' flyweight was found dead in his home at the age of 34 after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep

View 3 Images Allan Nascimento of Brazil was found dead at home

UFC fighter Allan Nascimento has been found dead at home at the age of 34.

‌



The Brazilian flyweight was pronounced dead after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep, the organisation has announced.

‌



A UFC statement said: “This morning, Monday, August 3, our beloved fighter and exemplary flyweight Allan Nascimento was found unresponsive after suffering an apparent heart attack in his sleep.

‌



View 3 Images LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JUNE 20: Allan Nascimento of Brazil prepares to face Mitch Raposo in a flyweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on June 20, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC)

“Despite the efforts of the responding medical team, he was pronounced deceased at the scene.

‌



“Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Allan’s family, friends, team-mates, and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.”

View 3 Images LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JUNE 20: (R-L) Mitch Raposo upnches Allan Nascimento of Brazil in a flyweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on June 20, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC)

Nascimento last fought in June, and had won a huge 22 of his 29 fights.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's opponents prepared to launch rival competition to force out FIFA boss

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is holding on by his finger nails, but his opponents are trying to get rid of him and are ready to take extreme steps to ensure that he is ousted

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino said the proposal will not proceed (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

The leaders of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC are ready to take extreme measures to oust FIFA boss Gianni Infantino - which includes setting up their own rival competition.

‌



The days of the FIFA president appear numbered in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup, but Infantino is determined to fight on. He's tried to lean on old acquaintances, but he's lost the faith of several of the world's major organisations.

‌



UEFA have been the most outspoken federation and have backing from other continental organisations. The Times reports that they're prepared to create their own tournament and UEFA have a blueprint for a global league having commissioned one in 2017, without using it.

‌



One source told the newspaper: “Everyone is very determined he needs to go, and if not we will take all the necessary steps [to remove him from power]. That includes future international competitions — would the big South American countries prefer to play France or Spain, or Lebanon or Djibouti? Everyone is very determined, there are no backward steps now.”

FA chiefs should be embarrassed by their prior support of disgraced Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump meeting not happening as third nation calls out FIFA boss READ MORE :

It remains feasible that Infantino will ignore the noise and try for re-election in March as he eyes a fourth term. Infantino’s opponents would therefore be prepared to impose a “governance boycott” which would see them refuse to take part in FIFA council or committee meetings.

A number of European associations, including England and Wales, have withdrawn letters of support for Infantino’s re-election after his World Cup sale plans fell flat. It comes after the FA had supported Infantino via a letter as recently as June.

‌



UEFA were outspoken against the FIFA president during the World Cup, heavily criticising his decision to suspended the red card handed to Folarin Balogun whilst their president Aleksander Ceferin refused to attend the final last month in New York.

View 2 Images UEFA strongly opposed FIFA's plans and want rid of Gianni Infantino (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

Europe's governing body has signalled its intent to take legal action after FIFA and said in a letter: “UEFA hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters.

Article continues below

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn makes seven-figure demand for latest star but admits he 'might not be the best'

England and Northampton star Henry Pollock is now managed by Matchroom and Eddie Hearn - who is seeking a record pay day for the player's next contract

View 2 Images Eddie Hearn is handling Henry Pollock's contract talks

Eddie Hearn has claimed that Northampton star Henry Pollock is "a seven-figure player" as he goes into contract talks with Northampton - even if the promoter admits "there might be players who are better".

‌



Pollock opted to join up with the Matchroom supremo several months ago and now has Hearn leading his contract negotiations with the Prem champions. The 21-year-old’s contract is thought to be around £150,000 per year, but it expires at the end of next season.

‌



Hearn is looking to land the England back rower a bumper pay day and has told Northampton to "recognise what they have got" whilst he stated that Pollock was "making an unquestionable difference to the bottom line of the club."

‌



The Matchroom chief is a hugely influential figure and has talked up the money Pollock could get if he chose to move elsewhere - and his financial demands would make Pollock comfortably the highest paid player at Franklin's Gardens.

Lewis Moody health latest as star arrives at Wimbledon after MND diagnosis READ MORE :

England strategy in the spotlight as Prem's best leaves and Exeter boss spells out reality READ MORE :

Hearn told the Telegraph: “It is all very well saying that there might be players who are a bit more consistent or might be better or whatever, but there aren’t players that are making an unquestionable and undeniable difference to the bottom line of the club.

‌



“Henry Pollock drives season ticket sales. Henry Pollock puts bums on the seats. Henry Pollock drives viewership on TNT or wherever it’s going to be. Henry Pollock sells shirts, right? That’s the difference. So you can actually put an economic value over having Henry Pollock on the team, and that has to be recognised, regardless of the want from Henry. He cannot stay at this club on the money that he’s on.”

Alongside his Northampton contract Pollock also receives around £150,000 per year from the Rugby Football Union as an enhanced elite player squad member with England. Northampton though have spent under the £6.4m cap with their marquee player thought to be fly-half Fin Smith.

View 2 Images Henry Pollock was recently with Eddie Hearn on his yacht (Image: @henryjpollock)

Article continues below

Reports claim Tommy Freeman will soon pen a deal that makes him the Prem's best paid winger but Hearn has talked up Pollock's financial pull off the pitch, even if the player would like to remain at Northampton. He also claimed the club's opening offer was not a “fair representation of his commercial value”.

“The first thing I said to Henry was: ‘Do you want to stay at Northampton?’” Hearn said. “And he said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘I love the club, I love the team, I love that I live 10 minutes away, and I think we’re going to win the championship again next year and I want to win championships'."

If Pollock wants to remain playing for England, which is the case, then he will have to sign with a club in the Prem. Many of those are already spending close to the cap and few would have the scope to pay a player £1m as things stand.

Sports.title: Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal
Sports.content:
Liverpool set for major cash injection as club enter advanced talks after £324m reveal

Liverpool are "working hard behind the scenes" and "pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people" ahead of this coming Premier League season starting

View 2 Images Liverpool could become the first Premier League club to expand their retail stores into the United States (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Liverpool are said to be in advanced talks to open permanent retail stores in the United States. No Premier League club has yet to launch any physical shops Stateside, with Manchester City coming closest, but only previously running pop-ups.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain are the pioneers in this regard across European football, opening their first store in Los Angeles five years ago and have since opened two more in Miami and New York City. The latter is their largest outside of France.

‌



PSG even expanded their presence on Fifth Avenue within 18 months. Liverpool now appear next in line to make the move.

‌



Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Liverpool's chief commercial officer Ben Latty told Sportico of Liverpool's ongoing discussions: "Clearly, we're not at the end of that because we haven't opened anything or announced anything yet, but I'd say we are pretty advanced in terms of speaking to the right people."

Liverpool have launched stores in Bali and London in recent months, with existing outlets already operating in Denmark, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Ireland, Singapore, South Africa and the United Kingdom.

The club's chief commercial officer is reportedly hopeful that their current tally of 26 stores will surpass 30 before the end of this season. Latty added: "We can't expect our numbers to grow organically.

‌



"We've got to work for them, and we've got to strategically put our investment where we think it's going to return the highest revenue for us as a club, so yeah, we are working hard behind the scenes."

View 2 Images Liverpool chief executive Billy Hogan spoke earlier this summer about the United States' importance (Image: John Powell, Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool's most recent accounts, filed for the 2024-25 campaign, reveal that their commercial income stood at £324million. Only City (£340million) and Manchester United (£333million) posted higher figures amongst Premier League sides.

‌



Speaking while part of this summer's fortnight-long pre-season tour, where the squad was stationed in Chicago, chief executive Billy Hogan said: "The US is a really important market from our perspective.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"A huge fan base here, over 26 million supporters of the club, which, I'm told, actually, the only US sports team that has more fans is the LA Lakers. So, a pretty good indication of the popularity of the club.

‌



"It's our number one international retail market. We are the number two most-watched team in European football here in the US. So, the team is incredibly popular.

"It's an important market from our perspective. (Almost 40 per cent) of our partners are here. And so, all of that kind of comes together to make it a super-important market from our perspective."

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu OUT of US Open as injury nightmare continues for British No.1

Emma Raducanu has been forced to skip the US Open due to a stress fracture in her lower right leg, having missed Wimbledon earlier in the summer

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu has been hampered by injuries recently (Image: Getty)

Emma Raducanu will miss a second consecutive Grand Slam tournament as she continues to recover from a stress fracture in her lower right leg.

‌



The world No. 49 is set to skip the US Open after pulling out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament earlier this summer.

‌



Raducanu, 23, has not played a match since finishing runner-up at the Queen’s Club almost two months ago. It’s now been five years since the Brit made history at the US Open, becoming the first and only qualifier to win a Major title.

‌



But on the half-decade anniversary of her heroic run, she will not compete in Flushing Meadows.

The US Open gets underway in less than four weeks, but Raducanu has already decided to skip the event on medical advice and is said to be sad to miss such a special tournament.

Since pulling out of Wimbledon, the British No. 1 has been spotted wearing a protective boot on her right leg. She has also shared footage from some early practice sessions. One video showed Raducanu sitting on a bin and hitting balls. In a second clip, filmed during a trip to Switzerland, she stood on a clay court and hit some serves.

‌



The US Open concludes on September 13, by which time Raducanu won’t have played a match for three months. She was also not named in Britain’s squad for the Billie Jean King Finals, which takes place in Shenzhen from September 22 to 27.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon less than 24 hours before her first round match (Image: Getty)

The world No. 49 also missed more than two months of competition from March to May due to post-viral illness, while a bone bruising injury in her foot wrecked her pre-season preparations. And the stress fracture is the latest issue to derail Raducanu’s 2026 season.

Article continues below

Announcing her withdrawal from Wimbledon on the night before her first-round match this summer, she said: “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but sadly I’ve had to withdraw from this year’s Wimbledon.

“I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.

“Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process. I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.”
