SRINAGAR: A suspect was arrested Monday in J&Kâs Pulwama with a hand grenade, three âanti-nationalâ posters and a mobile phone during a security overdrive spurred by last weekâs killings of two migrant labourers in a terror attack in neighbouring Kulgam.Police identified the man as Tousef Ahmad Dar, a local, and booked him under several laws, including the stringent Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Authorities claimed Dar was spotted walking towards a checkpoint set up jointly by J&K police, Army and CRPF and began to flee after noticing the security forces. Dar was chased down by troopers and caught some distance away, the police said.âThe police remain committed to maintaining peace and security and will continue to take firm action against individuals involved in anti-national and unlawful activities,â the police said in a statement.The checkpoint where Dar was spotted is one of many across Kashmir that have come up after the killings of the two migrant workers on July 31.Earlier, on July 23, a terrorist shot dead a J&K head constable, Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, in south Kashmirâs Anantnag. It was the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people, most of them tourists, dead on April 22 last year. The police said Lashkar-e-Toiba offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF) was involved in both the Kulgam and Anantnag attacks.On Monday, Kashmir IG VK Birdi reviewed security and ordered robust counter-insurgency measures. âHe (Virdi) stressed seamless coordination among all agencies. The IGP also reviewed security for highways, rail tracks and stations across the Valley. He directed officers to place âdynamic nakasâ and ensure enhanced foot patrolling, particularly at night, at vulnerable locations and inter-district boundaries,â a police spokesman said.

World.title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
World.content:
Deceased donor transplants still far short of demand

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisationâs (NOTTO) annual report. The figure marks a fourfold rise from 4,990 transplants in 2013.Delhi-NCR recorded the highest number of transplants in 2025 with 4,564 procedures, followed by Tamil Nadu (2,796), Maharashtra (2,136), Telangana (1,523) and Kerala (1,489). Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152).India has emerged as the worldâs third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China.India continues to rank first globally in living donor organ transplants, according to Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation report released in 2026.The 20,000-mark milestone coincided with the 16th Indian Organ Donation Day, when health ministry announced that more than five lakh Aadhaar-verified organ donation pledges have been recorded since the national digital pledge portal was launched in 2023.Despite the gains, deceased organ donation remains Indiaâs biggest challenge. Deceased donor transplants rose from 837 in 2013 to 3,526 in 2025, but continue to fall far short of demand. âA substantial gap still exists between demand for organs and their availability. Addressing this gap remains a national priority,â MoS for health Anupriya Patel said.To strengthen the programme, govt launched âJug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaanâ, a year-long awareness campaign, besides rolling out e-Pratyaropan, a digital platform for donor registration, waitlist management and organ allocation, NOTTO mobile app, and new Brain Stem Death Certification and Swap Transplantation guidelines.Govt has also expanded transplant services, with 10 new AIIMS now performing kidney transplants, while AIIMS Bhopal has started heart transplantation and AIIMS Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Patna, Rishikesh have launched liver transplant programmes.The report highlights reforms under âOne Nation, One Policyâ initiative, including removal of domicile requirements, the upper age limit and registration fees for patients seeking deceased donor organs. With nearly 1.73 lakh road traffic fatalities every year, the report says India has significant potential to increase deceased organ donation.

World.title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
World.content:
The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters.

Want to lay down norms on use of graded force, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for the dropping of cases against student protesters, Supreme Court on Monday permitted Delhi and state govts to withdraw or close FIRs lodged during NEET paper leak protests in different parts of India and said these youngsters must be allowed to pursue their studies without the fear of getting prosecuted.The bench clarified its July 28 order in which it had stayed coercive action against student protesters but permitted police to proceed with the investigations. This had created an apprehension in the minds of students about the future consequences of the cases remaining live.The go-ahead came after solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that âgovt is serious about honouring the commitment (given to CJP) on withdrawal of cases against student protesters. We are discussing the modalities of dropping casesâ.However, Mehta said that FIRs registered during student protests against 2,738 people who had criminal antecedents â having been accused of rape, murder and child sexual abuse under Pocso Act â and had infiltrated the protests to indulge in violence and vandalism will not be dropped. The bench said the rider would apply to those accused of heinous and grave offences and not petty offences or political cases.Mehta said, âThose who were leading the protests are again in touch with govt to work out the modalities for dropping cases against genuine student protesters as withdrawal of cases may not be possible under the law.â The top court posted the matter for further hearing on Aug 18.CJI Kant was firm that student protesters must be freed from the fear of future prosecution. He said, âParameters for students are altogether different. Their cases should be considered in a different manner so that they remain in the mainstream and their education is not disturbed.âThe parents are spending their hard-earned money on their childrenâs education. We must not keep aside the expectations of the parents of these youngsters. If the children are unnecessarily dragged into such (police and court) processes, it is not going to serve any purpose,â the CJI said.The solicitor general agreed and said modalities for the withdrawal/dropping of cases against student protesters will be worked out soon. He added, âThere will be some people who would like to keep the pot boiling â we must be very careful even while taking legal steps.âJustice Bagchi said that when the parties agree to it, the court can engender and enable the process so that the FIRs do not remain hanging over studentsâ heads.Senior advocate Vrinda Grover said both CJP leaders and other students are in talks with the SG and govt to chart out an agreed modality for the dropping of cases. She cited a Patna FIR registered against 142 people and 5,000 unknown persons, and said this appeared to be âcatch allâ tactics to pick up anyone randomly in the future. A comprehensive mechanism needs to be evolved, she said.Justice Bagchi said, âThere are many options. The prosecution can file a closure report, the public prosecutor can advise withdrawal of cases or we can quash the FIRs.âThe CJI-led bench said that while the violence and police excesses would be investigated by an SIT, âwe want to lay down comprehensive guidelines for the future on use of graded force, whether it should include pellet guns or not, after getting recommendations from the high-powered committee we intend to constituteâ.Senior advocate Shyam Divan said the committee/commission should be headed by a retired CJI. The bench said getting a former CJI to head the committee is difficult, and it will be chaired by a former SC judge. It asked Delhi Police, Centre and states to file their responses to the petition and give their suggestions on the terms of reference of the committee.Senior advocate N Hariharan questioned how Delhi Police could identify 2,738 criminals among the protesters and said they must have used face recognition devices on all protesters and profiled them, which is a serious violation of privacy of the individuals guaranteed under Article 21.

World.title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 â which will capture caste for the first time since 1931, and most likely also record the date and birthplace of parents, along with the respondentâs passport number (where available) and Aadhaar number (voluntary) â will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17.

A home ministry notification on Monday said the population enumeration exercise in snow-bound areas of the four northern states/UTs will run from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of August 17-30. This means that the questionnaire for Phase 2 of Census will also be notified soon.

According to sources, caste will be recorded âas declared by the respondentâ. There will be a drop-down menu for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the âcasteâ field will only cater to those in non-SC, non-ST category. The drop-down menu will only show the SC/ST list of the state where the respondent is being enumerated

The spelling of the declared âcasteâ will be recorded as cited by the respondent.

No document or caste certificate is required to be shown to verify oneâs SC, ST or âcasteâ status. An officer said while the self-declaration template followed for the socio-economic caste census (SECC) in 2011 had thrown up over 45,000 castes, making the data unusable, modern digital tools and AI can now surmount compilation and segregation challenges.

Census Phase 2, in a first, , will collect the date and place of birth of parents, the key factors that determine citizenship/nationality.





The national population register (NPR) exercise â conducted alongside Census 2011, intended to be repeated with Census 2021 before it was postponed, but now delinked from Census 2027 â had in 2010 collected details of nationality as declared by the respondent, with the rider that it would not confer any right of citizenship.

Sources said the respondents will not be asked for proof of birth details of parents and these would be recorded âto the best knowledge of the respondentâ.

In fact, where the respondents do not know the exact date of birth of parents but only the year, a default date like January 1 of that year will be accepted.

The Phase 2 questionnaire will also log passport details where available. Aadhaar number will be collected on a voluntary basis.

âThe purpose of collecting the birth data of parents is to know the total number of people who meet citizenship criteria based on their declaration, even though unverified.

It will have no impact on the individual as the Census Act does not allow individual data to be used for âlegal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,â said an officer.

Self-enumeration option for Phase 2, unlike Phase 1, may allow users to submit partially-filed enumeration forms, provided a minimum number of questions are answered. âThere is a realisation that even if some data fields are self-enumerated, the task of the enumerator becomes easier and less time-consuming,â said an officer.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As per convention, the population enumeration exercise â which records individual data like marital status, religion, SC/ST status, occupation, migration and fertility, besides arriving at the countryâs headcount â is conducted nationwide in February of the census reference year. However, it is advanced in pockets that face extreme cold and inclement weather during this window.

World.title: TVK lodges complaint against Udhayanidhi with NCW
World.content:
The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) lodged a complaint with the National Commission for Women against DMK youth wing secretary and Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin over his allegedly offensive remark, deemed to have been directed at a film actor, during a DMK demonstration in Thanjavur on August 3.

The complaint was lodged by Pazha Selvakumar, the party’s national spokesperson, seeking the intervention of the National Commission for Women. It urged the Commission to issue a notice seeking an explanation from Mr. Udhayanidhi and an unconditional public apology for his alleged remark, which was prompted by audience chants. The petition also sought directions to law enforcement authorities to initiate legal proceedings against him under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Several Ministers in the TVK-led government have condemned Mr. Udhayanidhi’s alleged remarks. The party has also announced protests against Mr. Udhayanidhi on Tuesday (August 4).

World.title: 22 children die of Chandipura virus in Gujarat this monsoon
World.content:
Twenty-two children have died due to Chandipura virus (CHPV) infection in Gujarat this monsoon season, with seven others currently undergoing treatment, State Health Minister Praful Panseriya said on Monday (August 3, 2026).

The State has reported 184 suspected cases of the virus so far, of which 35 have tested positive, while the results of 11 samples are awaited, the Minister said. All the affected patients are below 15 years of age.

Children admitted to civil hospitals in Gandhinagar, Himmatnagar, Patan, Rajkot and Bhavnagar are receiving specialised treatment, he said, adding that doctors are closely monitoring their condition.

Mr. Panseriya said the cases have been reported from different parts of the State and are not concentrated in any particular village.

To contain the spread of the virus, health teams are carrying out pesticide spraying in areas with animal husbandry activity to control sandflies, which transmit the virus.

The Health Department has instructed all government and private paediatric hospitals to immediately admit children showing symptoms of the infection to intensive care units with oxygen and ventilator support to prevent complications such as multiple organ failure.

Chandipura encephalitis is a viral disease that causes inflammation of the brain and is spread mainly by sandflies and other insects. The virus was first identified in 1965 in Chandipura village in Maharashtra’s Nagpur district.

World.title: Change in transgender law cannot take away rights already given, Supreme Court tells Centre
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) orally clarified to the Union government that a new law, seen as dismantling the transgender community’s right to self-identification, will not retrospectively, and by default, invalidate ‘transgender cards’ issued to members under a previous legislation.

Petitioners, who include activists and community members, pointed out that the importance of the transgender identity cards cannot be trifled away by the Union government.

A lawyer, who identified as a member of the community, said the card was an essential part of her basic identity.

“Every day I struggle. It is a struggle to even get a house to live in,” she told a three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench, replied that “we assure you, we are concerned about your rights”.

The petitioners have argued that the 2026 Amendment Act, which came into force on March 30, has dangerously allowed the state unfettered authority to determine gender identity.

They have contended that the 2026 Act has worked contrary to a NALSA judgment of the Supreme Court in 2014 which upheld transgender persons’ right to self-determined gender identity and protected them from discrimination and social stigma. The judgment had led to the enactment of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The 2019 Act had largely captured the essence of gender non-conformity and embodied the self-identification principle.

They submitted that Section 3 of the 2026 Act has omitted the right to self-perceived gender identity by the “stroke of a legislative pen”.

“Even if there is a change in legislation, the rights conferred or accrued must remain the same,” Justice Bagchi told the Centre, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta.

Lack of clarity

Mr. Mehta, seeking more time to respond to the petition, pointed out that lack of clarity about gender may lead to problems in succession and inheritance. He sought time to examine the law closely before responding to the petition.

The government law officer questioned the insistence on the part of the petitioners for a specific interim direction from the court to retain the validity of the transgender card.

“This is not like a ration card, where you do not get food,” Mr. Mehta said.

Justice Bagchi pointed out that had the legislative intent been to do away with the transgender cards, there would have been a clarificatory amendment. That was not the case in the 2026 statute.

Petitioners, including Laxminarayan Tripathi, who became the first transgender person from the Asia-Pacific region to address the United Nations General Assembly besides leading the first transgender participation in the Kumbh Mela, have asked “whether the state, through the instrument of legislation, may define who a person is, and in so doing, substitute its own biological or sociomedical classification for the lived, autonomous and self-perceived identity of a human being”.

World.title: Why has Parliament increased the number of Supreme Court judges? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far

The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, replacing an ordinance that increased the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India (CJI). The Bill was passed by voice vote without a debate amid Opposition protests over unrelated issues. It now awaits consideration in the Rajya Sabha.

What does the Bill do?

The Bill amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 to increase the number of puisne (ordinary) judges from 33 to 37. With the CJI included, the apex court’s sanctioned strength rises from 34 to 38.

This is the first increase in the court’s strength since 2019, when Parliament raised the sanctioned strength from 31 to 34 judges.

Why was the increase considered necessary?

The government has cited the growing backlog of cases in the Supreme Court.

As on January 1, 2026, 92,101 cases were pending before the apex court. In 2025, the court received 75,410 fresh cases but disposed of 65,615, despite functioning at nearly its full sanctioned strength.

According to the government, the persistent gap between the institution and disposal of cases has made it necessary to increase the number of judges.

What did the government tell Parliament?

Introducing the Bill in the Lok Sabha, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the increase in the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court was aimed at ensuring speedy and effective justice by enabling the apex court to deal with its growing workload.

The government has argued that the proposal was intended to address the mounting backlog of cases and improve the court’s disposal capacity. The increase in judicial strength, it said, was one of the “most exigent and viable solutions” to tackle pendency. It would also enable the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches more frequently to hear cases involving substantial questions of constitutional law without disrupting the hearing of regular matters.

How will additional judges help?

The government says the increase will enable the Supreme Court to hear more cases simultaneously, thereby improving the disposal rate.

One of the arguments in favour of additional judges is that it will make it easier for the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches on a regular basis.

The Constitution Benches, comprising at least five judges, hear cases involving substantial questions relating to the interpretation of the Constitution. Because of the heavy daily roster, constituting such Benches has often proved difficult.

Is increasing the number of judges enough to reduce pendency?

Most legal experts say it is a necessary step but not a complete solution.

Pendency is also linked to delays in judicial appointments, rising litigation, frequent adjournments, vacancies in High Courts and the subordinate judiciary, and the large number of appeals that reach the Supreme Court.

The backlog of cases across all courts in India had crossed 5.5 crore, with the bulk of them in the lower courts.

The India Justice Report, 2025, noted that there are 15.9 judges for every million Indians, as against a Law Commission of India recommendation of 50 judges per million in 1987.

In 22 of the 25 States, the same report noted, cases pending for over three years in subordinate courts amount to 25% of all cases pending.

And across 25 high courts, the number of cases which are pending for over five years accounts for 51%.

Experts have argued that improving case management, strengthening the High Courts and filling vacancies across the judiciary are essential to reduce pendency.

Why did the government promulgate an ordinance?

The Union Cabinet approved the proposal in May 2026, when Parliament was not in session. The government therefore promulgated an ordinance under Article 123 of the Constitution, allowing the increase in sanctioned strength to take effect immediately.

After the ordinance came into force, five judges were appointed against the enhanced sanctioned strength. Under the Constitution, an ordinance must be replaced by an Act of Parliament within six weeks of the commencement of the next session, failing which it ceases to operate. The Bill passed by the Lok Sabha seeks to replace that ordinance.

How has the Supreme Court’s strength changed over the years?

The Supreme Court began functioning in 1950 with eight judges, including the Chief Justice of India. Parliament has periodically increased its strength in line with rising litigation.

The sanctioned strength was increased to 11 in 1956, 14 in 1960, 18 in 1978, 26 in 1986, 31 in 2009, 34 in 2019, and now 38 (including the CJI) under the 2026 amendment.

What happens next?

The Bill must now be passed by the Rajya Sabha before being sent to the President for assent. Once enacted, it will replace the ordinance and formally fix the Supreme Court’s sanctioned strength at 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.

World.title: DU student alleges Meta restricted four CJP protest videos
World.content:
A Delhi University (DU) student, whose ‘Vasteganahuiyan’ video went viral during the Cockroach Janta Party protest, alleged on Monday that Meta had made at least four of her Instagram videos unavailable in India.

In an Instagram video, Sakshi said three videos were restricted citing 'community guidelines', while a post was removed for “adult sexual exploitation and nudity”.

The restricted videos included one in which she imitated a police announcement declaring something illegal, another showing a truck carrying food for police after the July 20 lathi charge, and one featuring members of Students’ Federation of India singing about youth unemployment.

She also said a video on Junaid — who gained fame for offering food to protesters at Jantar Mantar — and his family’s alleged treatment by the police had been affected.

A post containing three photographs showing clothes she alleged were torn by police personnel on July 20 was removed for “adult sexual exploitation”.

“I do not know which community guidelines have I violated. On the other hand, when I reported certain posts directed as hate reels at me, no action was taken,” she said.

World.title: Study links prolonged heat exposure during pregnancy to adverse birth outcomes
World.content:
A nationwide analysis of data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) quantifies the link between prolonged exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy and adverse birth outcomes in India. It was associated with a measurable increase in the risk of low birthweight, preterm birth and stillbirths among the mothers, and was tied to the trimester during which exposure occurred.

The paper ‘Effect of extreme heat stress on adverse pregnancy outcomes in India’, analysed 209,266 births recorded between 2015 and 2020, and matched each birth to local heat conditions during the pregnancy. It used nationally representative NFHS-5 data (2019–21) linked to high-resolution heat exposure estimates (India Heat Index) for 2015–20 across 707 districts. It uses ‘consecutive sweltering days’ instead of average temperature.

The researchers, Vineetha Vincent et al, showed that trimester-specific windows: heat extremes during the first trimester were most linked to preterm birth, the second trimester to low birth weight, and the third trimester showed a higher risk for stillbirth.

The risks were also higher among mothers with low Body Mass Index (<18.5), with lower education levels, and from poorer wealth groups, the study concluded.

It also found that urban residents showed slightly higher low birth weight rates than their rural counterparts.

Climate zones

The study also found associations between climatic zones, heat exposure, and pregnancy outcomes — mountainous zones showed stronger associations, while humid subtropical and arid zones also showed significant low birth weight occurrences. This is presented as the first population-scale evidence from India tying prolonged extreme heat stress (not just temperature) to adverse pregnancy outcomes, using a heat index that incorporates humidity, wind, and radiation.

The authors say research evidence already shows the potential biological effects of high ambient temperature: increased maternal core body temperature raises foetal core temperature, leading to birth defects, and dehydration decreases uterine blood flow and foetal growth, and due to reduced blood flow, there is a heightened chance of uterine contractions and an increased risk of preterm birth. Low and middle income countries experience higher birth rates and therefore, a larger absolute number of adverse birth outcomes.

The study was led by researchers at the University of Queensland – IIT Delhi Academy of Research, in association with the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (Centre for Atmospheric Sciences and School of Public Policy) and the University of Queensland’s School of Public Health, Brisbane, University of New South Wales, Sydney; the University of Exeter, U.K.; and Korea University, Seoul.

Strategies for future

With extreme conditions expected to increase due to global warming, India should prepare to address the heat challenges with more adequate adaptation planning, the authors say. It is crucial to raise awareness of the risks of heat exposure for pregnant women from marginalised populations, particularly those with lower education and in rural areas, they urge.

World.title: West Asia LIVE: Trump says new talks 'last chance' for Iran to forge deal, avoid escalation of U.S. strikes
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday (August 3, 2026) that negotiations with Iran were ongoing despite Tehran’s denials and the Islamic Republic was facing a “last chance before decapitation.” Mr. Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House, said he agreed to continue to pursue talks with Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and other countries.

Also read | Iran denies negotiating with U.S. after Trump announces talks

Mr. Trump said he expects negotiations will focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and create a pathway for Iran to address the United States’ concerns about its nuclear programme. He told reporters they would likely learn about the status of the negotiations “today or tomorrow”.

Also read | What’s at stake in the latest U.S.-Iran talks?

Iran’s Foreign Ministry denied on Monday (August 3) that negotiations with Washington were taking place, but Mr. Trump insisted they were. “We are talking right now,” he said. “Our negotiations are with Oman to secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz,” the critical oil corridor, Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

World.title: Fire breaks out at electronic chip unit in Noida, two firefighters killed, three injured
World.content:
A massive fire broke out at an electronic chip manufacturing unit in Noida, killing two firefighters and injuring three others, police said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

The incident occurred late on Monday (August 3) night at the ILGIM company in the Ecotech-3 industrial area, where at least six fire brigade vehicles were rushed after information about the blaze was received, a police spokesperson said.

The firefighters were attempting to douse the blaze when a wall and an iron beam inside the factory suddenly collapsed, injuring five of them, the spokesperson said.

All five injured firefighters were immediately taken to a hospital by ambulance, where Rohit Yadav and Tirathpal Singh succumbed to their injuries, he said.

The condition of the three other injured firefighters - Rajpal Singh, Manish Kumar and Amit Kumar - is stated to be out of danger and they are undergoing treatment, the spokesperson said.

Senior police officers, along with a team of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), are present at the spot, he said.

The cause of the fire is being investigated and necessary legal action is being taken, police said.

World.title: Pakistan to host Iranian officials as Trump’s patience wears thin
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US.

National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, meanwhile, invited his Iranian counterpart, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi. The invitations were delivered in Tehran late Monday night after Dar spoke with Araghchi.

“They exchanged views on regional and international developments, including the deteriorating situation in Occupied East Jerusalem,” the Foreign Office said in a statement.

It remained unclear when Ghalibaf and Araghchi would travel to Pakistan. A diplomatic source said both men had been asked to come as soon as possible for discussions on regional and international developments. Araghchi was in Iraq on Monday for Arbaeen, which is being observed on Tuesday.

The invitations came roughly 36 hours after US President Donald Trump announced he had canceled imminent strikes against Iran. Trump said allies had urged him to hold off because a deal appeared imminent.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump and persuaded him to call off the planned military action. Trump had also named UAE and Qatar as among the countries that had asked him to cancel the planned strikes.

Iran has been holding talks with Oman about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities say they are close to an agreement but have not indicated whether the waterway would reopen or remain closed.

Pakistan has been relatively quiet on the mediation front compared with earlier efforts that produced the Islamabad MoU. It has, however, remained engaged through back channels with Iran and, together with Qatar, proposed a ceasefire plan during a nearly 13-day period of escalation.

Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted that Pakistan is the main mediator with US. Spokesman Esmail Baqaei said: “The mediator in the discussions related to Iran and the US is Pakistan, and Qatar also helps in cases where necessary. To say that we have added a new mediator to the existing mediators is not, in the strict sense of the word, the case.”

Meanwhile, President Donald Trump accused Iran’s leadership of being “unbelievably duplicitous” after Tehran denied that any negotiations were underway with the US. The exchange renewed threats from Trump, who warned Iran faced “decapitation” and said he would keep up military pressure until there was a “deal, or total surrender”.

“I think we’re going to maybe get something, but I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump said, reiterating his threat to launch a major attack on Iran.

The war of words follows a familiar pattern in the five-month conflict between Washington and Tehran.

The president, who on Sunday said renewed talks would begin “tomorrow afternoon” without naming a venue or participants, added that the US Navy maintains complete control over the Strait of Hormuz.

“Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished,” he said.

Trump had told reporters aboard Air Force One that Iran, along with Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, had asked him to hold off on what he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”.

“Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people,” Trump said on Sunday. He described ongoing discussions as a “last chance for them to sign a good document”.

With input from Agencies

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs4.08, high-speed diesel by Rs2.45
World.content:
The government on Monday slashed the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.08 and Rs2.45 per litre, respectively, passing on the impact of falling oil prices after US President Donald Trump called off a planned attack on Iran and announced talks with it.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs331.95 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs389.93 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel.

The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 4 (Tuesday).

The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistan gets a pass on new US visa bond rule
World.content:
• Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded

• Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000

WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1.

The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not.

Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country.

The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent.

According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond.

Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”.

The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa.

The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays.

The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme.

The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific.

The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit.

The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa.

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: Heavy rain warning raises flood risk in low-lying areas
World.content:
• Medium to high flows expected in nullahs linked to Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi

• Authorities on high alert as NDMA reviews flood preparedness

LAHORE: While rising river flows have pushed Tarbela Dam near its maximum capacity, the Met Office has warned of urban flooding and inundation in low-lying areas of several cities as heavy monsoon rains are expected on Tuesday (today).

According to the Flood Forecasting Divi­sion (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological De­­­­partment, heavy rainfall may trigger wat­er accumulation in low-lying areas of Islam­abad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Faisalabad, Multan, Sahiwal, Okara, Bahawalnagar, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, the Potohar region, Peshawar and Nowshera.

The division also warned of flash flooding in hill torrents and local streams across Kashmir, Murree, Galiyat, northeastern Punjab, Islamabad, the Potohar region, some areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Dera Ghazi Khan. Medium to high flows are expected in nullahs linked to the Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi rivers, while flash floods are also likely in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Kabul River and its tributaries, and parts of northern Balochistan.

Landslides are also feared in the mountainous districts of upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Dir, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Shangla and Abbottabad, as well as Murree, Galiyat and the hilly areas of Azad Kashmir.

The FFD said the Indus River at Kalabagh, Guddu and Sukkur, and the Ravi at Balloki, are currently flowing at low flood level. It urged all relevant authorities to remain on alert and take precautionary measures to deal with possible rain-related emergencies.

According to the Water and Power Development Authority’s (Wapda) daily water report, the Indus at Tarbela recorded inflows of 250,700 cusecs and outflows of 191,900 cusecs on Monday. The Kabul River at Nowshera recorded both inflows and outflows of 43,700 cusecs, while the Jhelum at Mangla registered inflows of 44,700 cusecs and outflows of 7,000 cusecs. The Chenab at Marala recorded inflows of 85,900 cusecs and outflows of 69,900 cusecs.

The report showed that Tarbela Dam’s water level had risen to 1,543 feet, only seven feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,550 feet, with live storage reaching 5.178 million acre-feet (MAF). Mangla Dam’s water level stood at 1,199.35 feet, around 42 feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,242 feet, with live storage of 4.193 MAF.

Chashma Reservoir is also nearing full capacity, with its water level recorded at 648.50 feet against a maximum conservation level of 649 feet.

Monsoon, flood preparedness

Meanwhile, National Disaster Manage­me­­nt Authority (NDMA) Chairman retired Lt Gen Inam Haider Malik visited the Punjab Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) headquarters to review monsoon and flood preparedness across the province.

He was received by Punjab Minister Kha­waja Salman Rafique and PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa. The NDMA chairman visited the Provincial Emergency Control Centre, where officials briefed him on preparedness measures, while climate change, resource management and capacity building also came under discussion.

Mr Rafique said all departments, including health, rescue and livestock, were fully mobilised to respond to any flood emergency. He said Rescue 1122 had been equipped with modern equipment worth billions of rupees, while new warehouses were being established across Punjab to improve emergency response.

The NDMA chairman said the authority was maintaining close coordination with all provinces and that PDMA, Rescue 1122 and other institutions were responding effectively to the evolving monsoon situation.

The PDMA director general said officials were continuously monitoring river flows and the monsoon situation across the province. He said underground water storage tanks were being constructed to reduce urban flooding, while Wasa had been equipped with modern machinery and its operations expanded to 41 cities. During the visit, the NDMA chairman presented commemorative shields to Mr Rafique and Mr Jappa.

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: Govt executes agreements with pension fund managers
World.content:
• 16 companies to establish separate pension funds, ensure death and disability risk cover for employees

• Centre to establish non-banking finance company to assist in implementation, monitoring of pension scheme

ISLAMABAD: The government has executed agreements with 16 pension fund managers to formally operationalise the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme (DCPFS) launched a year ago for public sector employees as part of major pension reforms aimed at containing the snowballing pension burden on the budget.

In an announcement, the Ministry of Finance said it had executed agreements with 16 eligible pension fund managers, most of them banks and insurance companies. Around 10 of these eligible fund managers are owned or led by major commercial banks in the country.

They include ABL Asset Management Company, Al Habib Asset Management, Al Meezan Investment, Faysal Asset Management, JS Investments, MCB Investment, Alfalah Asset Management, HBL Asset Management, UBL Fund Managers and NBP Fund Management,

The pension fund managers led by or owned by insurance companies include EFU Life Assurance and Pak-Qatar Family Takaful. The remaining funds — Atlas Asset Man­agement, Lucky Invest­ments, National Investments and AWT Investments are owned by various business groups.

Under the agreements and rules, these fund managers would set up, operate and manage conventional or Shariah-compliant funds for state employees under the federal government-defined contributory pension fund scheme in accordance with the Voluntary Pension System Rules 2005.

Only these eligible pension fund managers shall be authorised to launch and manage employer pension funds for which the government will ensure annual budgetary allocation for the employer’s contribution. The agreements entail standard terms and conditions for providing systems support and electronic transfer of contributions to the pension fund’s designated bank accounts and further allocation of units to the relevant sub-funds in each employee’s pension account as per the allocation policy.

The agreements also envisage a mandatory insurance plan, providing death and disability risk cover to the employees, to be arranged by these fund managers.

The eligible pension fund managers will establish separate pension funds, while the government is responsible for the creation of a Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) to assist in implementation and monitoring of the pension fund scheme. Till such time the NBFC is established and fully operationalised, the government itself, through the finance ministry, will perform the NBFC role and establish an online portal to facilitate opening of pension accounts of employees, obtain information and data from eligible pension fund managers or otherwise communicate with the fund managers.

Under the rules, employees will not withdraw any amount from the pension account before retirement is notified. Even upon reaching retirement age, the employee shall not withdraw more than 25pc of the accumulated balance in the pension account, and shall invest the remaining amount in the manner prescribed in the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005, for a period of at least twenty years or till his death, whichever is earlier. However, the rules allow employees to transfer pension account balance from one eligible pension fund manager to another.

The government had announced pension reforms in 2024 to introduce a contributory pension fund for all government employees, including civil government and armed forces personnel. In a formal announcement in the National Assembly, the government said the contributory pension scheme would apply to all civil employees of the federal government, including civilian employees paid from defence estimates appointed on a regular basis on or after July 1, 2024. A September 2024 notification stated that the scheme would also apply to armed forces personnel appointed on or after July 1, 2025.

While the civilian side of the scheme has been implemented and the government has already set aside about Rs25bn for the scheme as its initial share, the contributory pension scheme for armed forces was deferred for a year to 2026 due to concerns over their peculiar nature of duties requiring detailed review, according to earlier statements by the finance minister and secretary.

Officials said the contributory pension scheme for armed forces personnel, which had been postponed two years ago, had been further delayed owing to internal departmental consultations and challenging security conditions, hindering any move that could be seen demoralising personnel.

The finance ministry notified in October 2025 that federal employees would contribute 10pc of their pensionable pay to qualify for a 12pc contribution from the public exchequer under the newly formalised contributory pension fund scheme. The total contribution rate will thus be 22pc, replacing the traditional pension system for new entrants. The October notification and pension rules superseded an earlier order of August 2024, which had set the government’s contribution at 20pc.

On Aug 20, 2024, the ministry initially announced the introduction of the contributory pension scheme for new entrants to the civil government and armed forces. At that time, employees were to contribute 10pc of their basic pay, while the government was to contribute 20pc.



The contributory pension scheme was introduced on the advice of international lenders, notably the World Bank, to contain the rising pension liabilities, which the government had itself described as a growing fiscal risk. It does not apply to existing employees but aims to slow future growth in pension liabilities. Federal pension expenditure is estimated at Rs1.170tr for FY2026-27, including about Rs860bn for military pensions and about Rs300bn for civil employees. The pension budget had increased from Rs1.055tr in 2025-26.

Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

World.title: Balochistan ‘not as bleak as portrayed’, says Bugti
World.content:
QUETTA: Balochistan Chi­­ef Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti has said that the sec­urity and governance situation in the province is neither entirely ideal nor as bleak as portrayed by some quarters outside the province.

He warned that negative and one-sided narratives are harming not only Baloc­his­tan but also Pakistan’s image and the government’s efforts.

In an interview with a private television channel, CM Bugti said the national media often focuses on Balochistan only when a violent incident occurs while overlooking the province’s progress, reforms, and development initiatives.

He said the provincial government had launched several youth welfare programmes, improved services at public hospitals, made all government schools functional, and recruited nearly 17,000 teachers through a transparent, merit-based process. However, he regretted that these achievements had received little attention at the national level.

The chief minister said the creation of new divisions and districts was intended to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of public services. He explained that some existing administrative units were too large to be managed effectively, making it difficult for the state to reach remote communities. Smaller administrative units, he said, would ensure better governance, quicker resolution of public issues, and greater public access to government services.

CM on security

Discussing the security situation, CM Bugti said Pakistan enjoys the support of the international community in its fight against terrorism. He alleged that anti-Pakistan terrorists groups were receiving support from Afghan territory despite commitments that Afghan soil would not be used against other countries. He further claimed that the facilitators, financiers, and trainers of various terrorist groups were linked to an Indian intelligence network.

He acknowledged that Balochistan’s vast geography, rugged terrain, long borders, and scattered population make counterterrorism operations more challenging. Nevertheless, he said security forces were conducting operations within the framework of the law while prioritising the protection of civilians.

CM Bugti criticised attempts by some political groups to associate terrorist incidents with the state, describing such narratives as harmful and misleading. He stressed that Baloch and Pashtun youth are patriotic and urged them to remain vigilant against hostile propaganda.

The chief minister said there were no successful international examples of negotiating with armed terrorist groups. However, he emphasised that dialogue with political parties, elected representatives, and young people remains essential for addressing political, administrative, and social issues.

Meanwhile, CM Bugti chaired a high-level meeting to review preparations for the upcoming Independence Day celebrations across the province. The meeting was attended by Corps Commander Balochistan, Lieutenant General Rahat Naseem Ahmed Khan, along with senior officials.

World.title: PCB moves IHC against orders to disclose players’ financial details
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Pak­istan Cricket Board (PCB) has approached the Islam­abad High Court (IHC), challenging two separate orders of the Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) directing the board to disclose extensive financial, contractual and operational information relating to national cricketers, selection committee members and other PCB officials under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017.

The petitions, filed through Advocate Kashif Ali Malik, are fixed for hearing before IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar.

The first petition challenges the PIC’s order of July 9, requiring the PCB to disclose its annual budgets for the financial years 2023 to 2025, along with a detailed breakdown of expenditure; policies governing the confidentiality and disclosure of such information; details of players and officials who travelled for this year’s T20 World Cup; and details of the board’s audit mechanisms and reports.

The second petition relates to information concerning Pakistan’s ODI series against South Africa held at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad, in November 2025. Through its order, the PIC directed the PCB to provide a breakdown of revenue, expenditure and details of steps taken or proposed to upgrade Iqbal Stadium for hosting PSL Season 12.

Board claims disclosure orders threaten commercial interests, privacy rights of players

Since taking office in 2024, PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi has stopped publishing the board’s financial statements on the PCB website. These statements had previously detailed expenditure across all departments, including the chairman’s office.

The PCB has contended that it operates in a highly competitive international sporting environment and, unlike government departments funded through the public exchequer, receives no funding from the federal government or the Consoli­dated Fund.

Instead, it says its revenues are generated primarily through commercial activities, including broa­dcasting rights, sponsorship agreements, media rights, gate receipts, licensing arrangements, international cricket events and distributions from the Inte­rnational Cricket Council.

In its petitions, the PCB argues that the impugned orders wrongly assume that all information sought is subject to disclosure under Section 5 of the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, while ignoring the Act’s express exemptions protecting personal privacy, confidential contractual arrangements, commercially sensitive information and third-party interests under Section 16. It contends that the information sought extends beyond institutional expenditure to confidential contractual and personal financial information of identifiable individuals, without recognising the distinction between institutional transparency and private financial affairs.

The PCB submitted that disclosure of confidential remuneration structures and contractual terms would prejudice its commercial interests and contractual negotiations.

The board also sought interim relief, arguing that once confidential contractual and personal financial information entered the public domain, the resulting prejudice to its commercial interests, contractual relationships and the privacy rights of third parties would be irreversible.

World.title: Senate body slams linking members to seizure of smuggled cigarettes
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control on Monday strongly condemned what it called a “malicious media campaign” targeting its members following the seizure of 11 trucks allegedly loaded with smuggled cigarettes on the motorway.

The meeting, convened by Senator Saifullah Abro at Parliament House, was mandated to scrutinise border security mechanisms, smuggling networks, anti-narcotics controls, and tax evasion, including an estimated $1 billion attributed to the tobacco sector.

The convener of the committee noted that after the July 20 meeting discussed the truck seizure, an official press release and handout were circulated the next day on TV channels targeting the committee chairman and members. The committee directed the Member of FBR to personally review the handout issued by his media wing and identify officials responsible.

The FIA has also been tasked with conducting a “completely impartial, full-scale inquiry” into TV channels running target­­ed smear campaigns and submit a report.

On the seizure of 11 trucks laden with smuggled cigarettes, the committee questioned jurisdiction, stating that Motorway operations fall under the Inland Revenue and not Customs.

It raised alarm over “contradictory valuation figures amounting to Rs220 million and ordered owners of the transport and steel company concerned to submit a full report by Monday evening.

It also questioned the legal basis of the FIR registered by Customs, noting that 11 truck drivers were arrested and produced in the court after a six-day delay.

The inspector who drafted the FIR has been summoned. The Deputy Collector of Customs was directed to explain why political figures present at the site were omitted from the official reporting.

The IG of Motorway Police clarified that an MoU exists with Customs only for “operational assistance in stopping suspicious vehicles”.

The committee expressed shock that manual consumption certificates are still being issued despite digital policy, and questioned whether physical verification visits are conducted before issuance.

It termed details provided on Rs1,120 billion of tax-exempted imports “completely unsatisfactory and incomplete” and ordered a comprehensive breakdown of local market sales against 2025-26 Quota Registration details.

The subcommittee reaffirmed its commitment to unearth malpractices across Customs posts, dry ports, and revenue bodies, and directed the FIA to finalise inquiries.
