Later, at the invitation of the Chinese branch of PEN International, a global association of writers founded in London in 1921, Shaw and other Chinese intellectuals visited the World College on Route Ferguson (now Wukang Road) to attend a gathering with local PEN members. When Shaw met Mei Lanfang, the renowned Peking opera artist and founder of Shanghai’s Left Theatre Club, he expressed his puzzlement over the differences between Eastern and Western theater.

“Will you please tell me how a Chinese actor can do anything in the midst of such infernal uproars as one hears on your stage?” he asked. “In our theater, they put a man out if he sneezes. But you have gongs and cymbals and the competition of half the audience and innumerable vendors. Don’t you object?”

Mei explained that Peking opera was a folk art first performed in the open air, and drums and gongs were then used to attract people to the show. This tradition had simply endured.

Around 3 p.m., Shaw finally spoke with some Chinese and foreign reporters in the garden of Soong’s residence, discussing socialism, national oppression, Eastern culture, and revolutions, among other topics. Afterward, Soong accompanied Shaw back to the Empress of Britain, which then carried the playwright northward to Beijing.

Although Shaw spent just over eight hours in Shanghai, his visit sparked considerable discussion and reverberations among the city’s left-wing intellectual circles. The writer and poet Yu Dafu wrote in Free Talk, a supplement of the Shun Pao newspaper, that he hoped Shaw could tell the world, in his own sarcastic tone, about Japanese imperialism and its invasion of China.

At the time, intellectuals including Lu Xun and the poet and translator Qu Qiubai were working to build a central stronghold for China’s left-wing cultural movement. After Shaw’s departure, they, along with partners Xu Guangping and Yang Zhihua, began compiling reports from various newspapers and periodicals about the Irish novelist’s short visit. The collection was published in March 1933 by Yecao Shudian, or Wildgrass Bookshop, under the title “George Bernard Shaw in Shanghai.”

In the preface, Lu wrote: “Those who truly welcomed him were the Chinese people, as well as the literary and artistic circles that stood by the people. The Chinese people did not regard him as a ‘revolutionary leader’ or a ‘thoroughgoing socialist writer,’ much less as an idol. They regarded Shaw as a loyal friend of the oppressed people of the world, and of China.”

Editor: Hao Qibao.

(Header image: Visuals from the Shanghai Lu Xun Museum, reedited by Sixth Tone)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018830/How Cantonese Cuisine Became Part of the English Language
World.title: How Cantonese Cuisine Became Part of the English Language
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018830/How Cantonese Cuisine Became Part of the English Language
World.content:
This is the first article in a two-part series exploring how Chinese culinary terms came to be included in the Oxford English Dictionary (OED).

For more than two decades, I have studied how Chinese words enter the English language, particularly through food. So when the Oxford English Dictionary (OED) released its second batch of updates this past June, one updated entry felt especially meaningful to me: “Cantonese.” For the first time, the dictionary formally recognized the word as a culinary term, defining it as food prepared in the style of Guangzhou and the surrounding region in southern China, as well as the restaurants that serve such cuisine.

The entry is accompanied not just by a simple definition, but by a timeline of citations tracing the term’s culinary history. The earliest example dates back to April 6, 1892, when New Jersey’s Trenton Times referred to “Fashionable Cantonese dishes.” This phrase shows that the term was already being used in relation to food more than a century ago, long before the era of modern globalization.

Western interest in Cantonese cuisine also stretches back to the late 19th century. The OED cites an 1894 report from The Washington Post describing a dim sum dumpling as “shaped exactly like a fishing creel.” By 1908, The New York Herald was explaining the dish to its readers by comparing it to a “second cousin to steamed sponge cake.” These early descriptions reveal how unfamiliar foods were introduced to Western audiences through comparisons with things they already understood.

Over the following decades, Cantonese cuisine continued to leave its mark. A 1950 publication by the Hong Kong Young Women’s Christian Association highlighted “Cantonese specialties” such as turnip pudding, while a 1997 culinary memoir recalled dining at a large “Cantonese restaurant” where dim sum was served from rolling trolleys. More recently, a 2015 article in The Guardian recommended Wong Chi Kee in Hong Kong for its “traditional Cantonese congee.”

These citations connect to a broader ecosystem of existing terms. The Cantonese practice of yum cha, literally “drinking tea,” the social meal of dim sum and tea traditionally enjoyed in the morning, was added to the dictionary in 2016, while dim sum has appeared in the dictionary since 1989.

Today, my research shows that the dictionary contains a vocabulary of 25 Cantonese culinary terms. Beyond the widely recognized dim sum and yum cha, the list includes char siu, wonton, chop suey, hoisin sauce, egg foo yung, and moo goo gai pan. These are no longer treated as foreign concepts requiring lengthy explanations; they have become established English words.

Yet this lexicographical milestone is not simply a retrospective look at history; it also reflects a living culture. Just months earlier, in March 2026, three new additions expanded the OED’s Cantonese culinary vocabulary: dan tat (egg tart), pineapple bun, and yin yeung (a Hong Kong drink combining milk tea and coffee). Their inclusion highlights that Cantonese cuisine is not a static relic of the past. It continues to evolve, innovate, and influence the English language. This ongoing linguistic exchange shows that the relationship between East and West remains an active and continuing process.

The contrast with other regional Chinese cuisines highlights that global influence is not simply a product of modern international presence. Shanghai, for instance, is one of China’s most globally connected cities, yet its local Benbang cuisine has left far fewer traces in the English language. Cantonese cuisine’s deep roots in English developed instead through generations of migration, trade, and everyday use.

Etymologically, “Cantonese” derives from “Canton,” the former English name for Guangzhou, which was first recorded by Portuguese traders in the 16th century. Over time, the term evolved from a geographic reference into a marker of a distinct cultural and culinary identity. This reflects a broader historical reality: Cantonese cuisine established an overseas presence earlier than many other regional Chinese cuisines, spreading through centuries of maritime trade and migration.

Historically, because the vast majority of early Chinese immigrants to many Western countries came from Guangdong, Cantonese restaurants dominated many Chinatowns. Iconic establishments such as New York’s Port Arthur Restaurant, which opened in 1897 and introduced upscale Cantonese dishes to Western diners, and San Francisco’s Shanghai Low, a Cantonese restaurant that adopted a Shanghai-inspired name to appeal to Western customers, did more than serve food. They became gathering places for immigrant communities and helped establish Cantonese cuisine’s prominence in Western societies.

As a linguist, I often argue that translation is not merely a tool for communication between languages; it is also a means of cultural understanding. The inclusion of these terms shows that English speakers are capable of adopting culinary vocabulary from other languages on its own terms.

For readers interested in exploring this vocabulary, here are eight popular Cantonese culinary terms currently included in the OED, with condensed definitions for clarity.

Many of the early Cantonese restaurants that introduced these dishes to Western audiences have since disappeared. Yet the vocabulary they helped popularize has endured, and a new generation of Cantonese restaurants continues to thrive in Chinatowns and communities around the world. The OED’s recognition of Cantonese cuisine reflects this longer history of cultural exchange: carried across borders by generations of immigrants, Cantonese food has become a lasting part of the global culinary vocabulary.

World.title: [Vantage Point] The fire Marcos started, and the signature at the bottom
World.content:
Suitcase testimony can explain the mechanics, but bank records, property purchases, foreign-exchange transactions, corporate ownership, and communications must supply corroboration

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. deserves one presumption that critics have been reluctant to grant him: a president knowingly profiting from the flood-control racket would have taken an extraordinary risk when he publicly set the scandal ablaze.

During his 2025 State of the Nation Address, Marcos ordered officials to expose failed, substandard and possibly fictitious flood-control projects. “Mahiya naman kayo sa mga kabahayan nating naanod o nalubog sa mga pagbaha,” (“Have you no shame for our countrymen whose homes were swept away or submerged by the floods?”) he thundered, before rebuking those who would leave the resulting debts for Filipino children to pay.

A year later, the fire reached his family. Marcos told the nation that the expected prosecution of his cousin, former House speaker Martin Romualdez, pains him but the investigation must proceed. He declared, “Hindi ako ang Pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako ang Pangulo ng aking mga kaibigan. Ako ang Pangulo ng Pilipinas.” (“I am not the President of my family. I am not the President of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines.”)

Romualdez answered: “Masakit man ito sa aming pamilya, iginagalang ko ang naging pahayag ng Pangulo. Hindi ako kailanman humingi ng pabor o espesyal na pagtrato. Sang-ayon ako na gawin natin ang tama.” (“Although this is painful for our family, I respect the President’s statement. I have never asked anyone for favors or special treatment. I agree that we must do what is right.”) He added that due process should be followed, the evidence allowed to speak, and his innocence tested fairly.

That exchange complicates the easy narrative that Marcos and Romualdez are staging a family drama to protect themselves. The 104-page supplemental complaint filed before the Ombudsman against Romualdez is hardly cosmetic. It accuses him and former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co of conspiring to amass approximately P56 billion between 2022 and 2025 through alleged kickbacks, bribery, graft, and money laundering connected with government projects. (READ: [Rappler’s Best] Mahiya naman kayo)

Investigators cite public works officials, security personnel, and couriers who allegedly transported cash in suitcases, together with corporations and intermediaries supposedly used to transfer or conceal assets. (READ: Martin Romualdez properties: Where and how much?)

Still, accusation must not be confused with conviction. The complaint is for preliminary investigation. Romualdez may submit counter-affidavits, challenge witnesses, and contest the documents.

If the Ombudsman finds probable cause, it may file criminal information before the proper court. Only then may a judge independently determine whether probable cause exists to issue a warrant of arrest. Marcos may support the process, but neither he nor the Ombudsman can guarantee its outcome.

Powerful objection

Critics nevertheless raise a powerful objection: every national budget from which the alleged racket drew nourishment carried Marcos’s signature. The budget begins inside the executive branch through the National Expenditure Program, passes through Congress, and returns to Malacañang for item approval or veto.

Once enacted, executive agencies control releases, bidding, implementation, and inspection. Politically, Marcos owns those budgets. A President who claims credit for classrooms, bridges, and hospitals financed by the General Appropriations Act (GAA) cannot become a spectator when appropriations turn out to be fictitious, overpriced, or corrupted.

But political responsibility is not synonymous with criminal guilt. A presidential signature on a multitrillion-peso budget does not prove that Marcos knew a flood-control project was fictitious, approved a kickback, protected its collectors, or received proceeds.

No President personally inspects thousands of drainage systems, seawalls, and river projects before signing the GAA. Appropriation merely authorizes expenditure; it does not establish participation in a conspiracy.

Here, Marcos deserves the benefit of the doubt. His decision to expose the anomalies appears inconsistent with guilt. If he knew that a genuine investigation would lead back to him, why invite the public, Congress, auditors, and law-enforcement agencies to dig deeper into the projects?

Why create the political conditions that forced Romualdez from the speakership and placed his cousin before the Ombudsman? A conspirator normally suppresses records, protects participants, and redirects scrutiny. Marcos did the opposite, at least publicly.

This is persuasive evidence of good faith, but not conclusive. Politicians sometimes launch controlled investigations, believing they can contain the damage, sacrifice participants, or direct attention away from themselves.

Marcos may also have underestimated the scheme or assumed the trail would stop below Malacañang. The fire he started could have escaped its intended perimeter. These are possibilities, not proof, and fairness requires that suspicion should not become culpability merely because critics distrust him.

Reasonable doubt

The test must provide the evidence. Marcos’s defense weakens if project lists originated from presidential offices; if close aides transmitted instructions or received collections; if warnings reached him before budget approval or fund release; or if financial records connect proceeds to him, his family or controlled entities.

Conversely, his defense strengthens if anomalous items can be traced to congressional alterations, rogue officials, and contractors acting without his knowledge, and if he gives investigators complete, continuing access to records even when the trail reaches allies.

The Ombudsman must therefore reconstruct the scheme project by project: who proposed each appropriation, who altered it, which contractor benefited, what percentage was demanded, who collected the cash, and where did the fund go?

Suitcase testimony can explain the mechanics, but bank records, property purchases, foreign-exchange transactions, corporate ownership, and communications must supply corroboration. (READ: [Inside the Newsroom] Properties, patterns keep leading back to Martin Romualdez)

The fairest judgment is that Marcos stands inside the chain of political accountability, but has not been shown to stand inside the criminal conspiracy.

Although his signatures warrant scrutiny, his decision to trigger the investigation casts reasonable doubt on his guilt.

The pivotal issue shifts from determining who started the fire, but whether the President will allow it to burn wherever the evidence leads, even if it implicates Romualdez or ultimately consumes Malacañang.

I welcome your views on these and other issues where decisions made in power shape the country’s economic future.

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

World.title: Laptops vs lapel mics: Teachers’ groups hit Marcos’ unfulfilled SONA promise
World.content:
LAPEL MIC. The Department of Education provides lapel microphones for public school teachers.

More than a year since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s promise in his 2025 SONA, the Department of Education says the procurement process for over 250,000 laptops for teachers is almost complete

MANILA, Philippines – Teachers’ groups are calling out President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for the still unfulfilled promise of laptops for them, as they instead received lapel microphones in recent days.

In separate statements on Monday, August 3, the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) and the Teachers’ Dignity Coalition (TDC) said laptops remain their most needed gadget, not lapel mics or voice amplifiers.

Marcos promised the delivery of laptops to every public school teacher during his 2025 State of the Nation Address (SONA).

In his 2026 SONA last July 27, the President also said the government would continue to provide “helpful and innovative teaching aids, such as smart TVs, laptops, tablets, free mobile data, and even lapel microphones.” Days after, several schools posted on social media that they had received the lapel mics.

In a statement on Sunday, August 2, the Department of Education (DepEd) clarified that procurement processes for the two items are separate.

“Lapel now. Laptops next…. Nauna lang ang voice amplifiers habang isinasagawa ang procurement ng teacher laptops upang matiyak ang tamang performance, durability, battery life, warranty, at [pinakamainam] na halaga para sa mahigit 250,000 units. Malapit nang matapos ang procurement process,” the DepEd said.

(Lapel now. Laptops next. We provided the voice amplifiers first as we continue to conduct the procurement of teacher laptops to ensure proper performance, durability, battery life, warranty, and the best price for over 250,000 units. The procurement process is almost complete.)

The lapel mics for nearly 880,000 teachers nationwide were bought using the President’s Social Fund, according to the video message of Education Secretary Sonny Angara played during distribution ceremonies in schools.

“Gamitin po natin ito. Alagaan din po natin ito dahil ito’y biyaya…. At para sa ating mga estudyante ito,” Angara said.

(Let’s use this lapel microphone. Let’s also take care of it because it’s a blessing. It’s for the benefit of our students, too.)

The DepEd said competitive bidding led to a lower unit price for the voice amplifiers, from the approved P480.76 ceiling to around P300 to P370, depending on location. The units have a one-year warranty.

However, ACT reported that it received feedback from teachers that the lapel microphones were of “poor quality, with weak audio output,” and some units have supposedly malfunctioned or stopped working after being used just once. Rappler has sought comment from the DepEd.

While the lapel mics may be of use due to congestion in schools, ACT said providing such items is only a stopgap measure.

“Instead of easing teachers’ burden through smaller class sizes, more classrooms, and additional teaching personnel, the government has resorted to temporary measures while many schools, particularly in urban centers, continue to hold classes of 40 to more than 50 learners,” ACT chairperson Ruby Bernardo said.

What happened to laptops?

The two teachers’ groups also hit the government for the insufficient number of laptops slated for distribution.

“Ang kagamitang dapat sana’y ipinagkakaloob ng pamahalaan ay nagiging karagdagang pasanin pa ng mga overworked at underpaid na guro,” TDC national chairperson Benjo Basas said.

“Kung nakapaglalaan ang gobyerno ng mga baril at bala para sa mga pulis at militar upang magampanan ang kanilang tungkulin, bakit hindi rin ito makapaglaan ng laptop para sa mga guro?”

(The equipment that should be provided by the government becomes an additional burden for overworked and underpaid teachers. If the government can provide guns and ammunition to police and the military so that they can do their duty, why can’t it give laptops to teachers?)

Basas also said this puts into question the administration’s credibility, accountability, and sincerity in making promises.

In Marcos’ 2025 SONA, he also vowed the procurement would be free from anomalies.

In 2023, Rappler found that negligence and apparent corruption at the DepEd under the Duterte administration caused laptops intended for public school teachers to end up being sold in retail stores.

Other DepEd actions

Following the recent SONA, the DepEd said it is working with the budget department to secure P12 billion for the promotion of teachers and school heads under the Expanded Career Progression System for 2027.

It said it is still filling nearly 33,000 new teaching positions and more than 32,000 non-teaching posts, specifically school counselor associates, administrative officers, project development officers, and school principals.

The DepEd added that it is digitizing 10 school forms to “streamline documentation, reporting, and school data management.” Teachers have long raised the issue of excessive and repetitive administrative paperwork. – Rappler.com

World.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ debut sets all-time US, Canada box-office records
World.content:
DANCE. A person dressed as Spider-Man dances with a member of the New York Mets Queens Crew prior to the game against the Miami Marlins at Citi Field.

Around the globe, the movie brought in a total of $932 million in ticket sales, the second highest-grossing total in cinema history

LOS ANGELES, USA – “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” set an all-time record at US and Canadian movie box offices over the weekend, snagging $360 million to top the milestone set by 2019 superhero blockbuster “Avengers: Endgame,” according to ticket sales data released by Sony Pictures on Monday, August 3.

Around the globe, the movie brought in a total of $932 million in ticket sales, the second highest-grossing total in cinema history.

On Sunday morning, August 2, Sony’s estimates suggested the new “Spider-Man” adventure would finish second domestically behind the Avengers movie, which opened with $357 million before adjusting for inflation. The day’s ticket sales came in higher than expected to lift “Spider-Man” to the top of all-time box office charts, without accounting for inflation.

CAST. Director Destin Daniel Cretton poses with cast members Sadie Sink, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Krondon, Michael Mando, Liza Colon-Zayas, Tramell Tillman, and Jon Bernthal as they attend the world premiere for the film Spider-Man: Brand New Day in Los Angeles, California, US, July 27, 2026.

The movie, which marks actor Tom Holland’s fourth appearance in a Spider-Man movie, depicts Peter Parker fighting crime in a world that has forgotten he is Spider-Man. Zendaya co-stars as MJ, the love of Parker’s life. Audiences returned for a film that was grounded in Parker’s struggles with loneliness and his pursuit of human connection.

“‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is fundamentally a movie about friendship, about the balm of connection in all our lives, and that is resonant to audiences of all ages and all around the world,” Tom Rothman, chairman and chief executive of Sony Pictures Entertainment’s Motion Picture Group, said.

When adjusting for inflation, “Avengers: Endgame” still ranks as No. 1. The film brought in an inflation-adjusted $1.6 billion in global ticket sales over its opening weekend in 2019, including $467 million in the US and Canada.

Spider-Man is one of the most popular of Marvel’s comic book characters, with a cinematic appeal that endures even as audiences have shown signs of fatigue with the superhero genre. The latest installment has been well-received, scoring a 90% rating from critics and 98% approval from moviegoers on Rotten Tomatoes.

Paul Dergarabedian, head of marketplace trends for Rentrak, said on Friday, July 31, that the franchise is approaching the $10 billion mark in unadjusted worldwide theatrical box office, which speaks to the character’s appeal.

Greg Durkin, the founder and CEO of the entertainment research firm Enact Insight, said the movie’s central themes of loneliness and isolation, and triumphing over drama, resonated especially with Gen Z filmgoers.

“There’s a mental health crisis now with young people in our country — it’s especially acute for young men right now. There’s a friendship crisis,” Durkin said. “The pandemic created a bunch of shock-wave effects that we haven’t fully documented, much less addressed. This movie touches on some really important themes.”

The performance of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” fuels an already-robust summer box office, which has been buoyed by such major releases as “Toy Story 5” and “The Odyssey.”

Dergarabedian said on Sunday that the combination of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” with another hit, “The Odyssey,” created the “all-time biggest domestic weekend” in movie theaters.

“There’s no better lead-in to this movie than ‘The Odyssey,'” Dergarabedian said. “Think of how many people around the world were in movie theaters being exposed to trailers marketing for ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day.'”

Holland, Zendaya and Jon Bernthal appear in both movies.

The overall domestic box office performance remains below pre-pandemic levels. Year-to-date receipts are up 10% from last year, but 16% below 2019, the year before the pandemic struck, according to Rentrak. – Rappler.com

World.title: Wildfires in Washington state destroy over 700 buildings, force 64,000 to flee
World.content:
A firefighter works to put out a fire at a home as a wildfire burns in Spokane County, Washington, U.S., August 1, 2026, in this still image taken from bodycam video. Spokane County Fire District 8 Firefighters Local 3711/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. MANDATORY CREDIT

The Spokane-area fires have scorched more than 3,200 hectares since erupting on the northern fringe of the city, home to about 230,000 residents west of the Rocky Mountain foothills near the Idaho border

WASHINGTON, USA – Wildfires raging on the outskirts of Spokane, Washington, for a third day have destroyed at least 700 buildings and forced tens of thousands of people to flee their homes in and around the state’s second-most populous city, officials said on Monday, August 4.

The cluster of three blazes ranked as the top firefighting priority in the US as a whole, including the drought-parched Pacific Northwest, where dozens of major wildfires have been burning for weeks, degrading air quality across a wide region.

The Spokane-area fires have scorched more than 3,200 hectares since erupting on Saturday, August 1, on the northern fringe of the city, home to about 230,000 residents west of the Rocky Mountain foothills near the Idaho border.

Video footage from the fire zone showed a kilometers-long column of smoke creeping through treetops as airplane tankers swooped overhead, dropping scarlet-colored fire-retardant slurries onto the blaze.

Enormous palls of smoke billowed into the sky north of the city, as flames devoured forest land 10 km from Spokane’s downtown. Elsewhere, suburban homes lay in smoking ruins among charred trees. Other video showed fires burning along wooded ridge lines above adjacent dwellings.

As of Monday, some 64,000 people were under immediate evacuation orders, up from 4,000 a day earlier, according to Benjamin Cossel, a spokesperson for the incident command center.

At least 700 structures have gone up in flames, mostly in residential areas, and aerial infrared surveys showed that possibly another 400 buildings, including homes, had been damaged or destroyed, Cossel said.

The cause of the blazes was under investigation.

Bracing for fatalities

“There are just so many Washingtonians who have literally lost everything in a very, very short period of time,” Governor Bob Ferguson said at an afternoon press briefing. “In a matter of hours, their lives changed in deeply dramatic and fundamental ways.”

No injuries or fatalities have been reported so far, Cossel told Reuters, adding, “There’s a high probability that will change in the coming days” as flames subside and search teams are able to reach devastated communities still inaccessible due to extreme fire activity.

An unspecified number of people have been reported missing as flames spread out of wooded areas into neighborhoods and commercially developed areas, “turning from a wildfire to an urban conflagration,” he said.

“We are still assessing the potential for lives to be lost,” Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown said at the news conference.

Body-mounted camera footage showed firefighters rushing from house to house in one wooded neighborhood, dousing fires that sprang up around homes.

Roughly 1,100 firefighters were battling the Spokane blazes as of Monday, Cossel said, a fraction of the more than 29,200 personnel assigned to wildfires nationwide, most heavily concentrated in Oregon, Washington state and Idaho, according to the National Interagency Fire Center in Boise.

The agency reported more than 100 large new wildfires on Sunday across 15 states, the bulk of them in the Northwest, stretching resources thin across the region.

The Spokane cluster was one of 15 major fires burning in Washington state alone, with more than 250,000 acres ablaze, according to state Public Lands Commissioner Dave Upthegrove.

“This is an extraordinary wildfire season in the Pacific Northwest,” he told reporters.

‘Explosive’ fire behavior

North of the US-Canadian border, flames continued to rage across British Columbia, where record drought conditions have led to what officials over the weekend called “explosive” fire behavior in the southern part of that province.

Aerial firefighting assets in Spokane were so far limited to four fixed-wing tanker aircraft, with no water-dropping helicopters currently available, Cossel said.

Fire managers hoped their crews could make greater headway during a narrow window of cooler, less windy weather expected to prevail on Monday and Tuesday, before extremely high temperatures, low humidity and gusty conditions are forecast to return at midweek, Cossel said.

Even though fire activity in some spots has eased in comparison with Sunday, authorities were reluctant to lift evacuations in most of the fire zone.

“The worst thing in the world is to let people go home only to have to evacuate them again 24 to 48 hours later,” Cossel said.

As of Monday, firefighters had gained zero containment around any of the three Spokane-area blazes, officials said.

The Interagency Fire Center has documented a total of 44,722 wildfires year to date nationwide, the highest number for this time of the year in at least a decade, with nearly 5.2 million acres consumed, the most from January to early August since 2022.

The conditions driving the increase in wildfire activity in North America, Europe and elsewhere in recent years, especially periods of prolonged drought and extreme heat, are largely a function of human-caused climate change, according to scientists. – Rappler.com
